name: cp-audit
description: Проводит аудит аккаунта по девяти слоям: упаковка, позиционирование, контент, хуки и входы, воронка, продажи, производство, правовой контур РФ (реестр блогеров, маркировка, персональные данные) и доступность данных. По каждому слою — что смотрим, признаки проблемы, что чинится за вечер и что требует перестройки. Отчёт начинается с трёх вещей, которые уже работают, дальше 5–7 находок с приоритетом в формате «нашёл → что делать → сколько времени». Результата от исправлений не обещает: называет точки потерь. Триггеры — «аудит аккаунта», «разбор блога», «почему не растёт», «посмотри мой профиль»,…

Сначала оценивает экономию времени, затем строит сценарий с повторами, защитой от дублей и обработкой ошибок. Диалоги бота ведёт cp-bot. Use when the user wants to automate a workflow, connect services, build a no-code scenario, schedule publishing, or collect stats automatically. Триггеры — «автоматизация», «n8n», «интеграция сервисов», «сценарий без кода», «вебхук», «автопостинг», «перенести данные между сервисами», «отчёт автоматом», «собирать статистику автоматически», «свя…

Даёт архитектуру «триггер → условие → действие → обработка ошибок → уведомление» с обязательным блоком повторов и защиты от дублей, который в самодельных автоматизациях отсутствует чаще всего. name: cp-be

It probes the models' ability to integrate linguistic content with emotional, prosodic, and social cues from in-the-wild speech data to answer specific question types. Use when the user wants to benchmark on CP-Bench, or asks about evaluating this task. Reports LLaMA-3-70B judge score.

Даёт каркас прогрева из пяти касаний с сегментными развилками, технические правила deeplink и триггер-слов, разбор новых возможностей Bot API и обязательный правовой блок по сбору контактов. Use when more than ~30 exchanges have passed without compaction, before major direction changes, preparing to end a session, or when memory exceeds ~1500 words. name: cp-compliance

Отдаёт чек-лист с вердиктом по каждому пункту: можно, нельзя, уточнить у юриста. Конкретные суммы штрафов и ставки не берёт из памяти, а требует сверки на текущую дату. Use when the user asks whether something is advertising, needs erid marking, may be published in Russia,…

Разделяет searchable, который ловит существующий спрос в поиске, и shareable, который создаёт спрос в рекомендательных лентах. Приоритизирует скорингом: влияние на клиента 40%, соответствие бренду 30%, поисковый потенциал 20%, стоимость производства 10%. Держит пул из десяти готовых тем вместо жёсткого расписания и показывает перекосы по аватарам, пилларам, форматам и стадиям воронки числами. Триггеры…

name: cp-e2e

name: cp-editorial

name: cp-editorial-review

name: cp-email
description: Строит рассылки по собственной базе — приветственную серию, регулярную, продающую и реактивацию — и отвечает за инженерную часть: аутентификацию домена SPF, DKIM и DMARC, прогрев отправителя, сегментацию по вовлечённости и пошаговую диагностику падения доставляемости. Применимо и к почте, и к рассылкам в мессенджерах и сообществах, с оговоркой, где механика различается. Прогрев внутри диалога чат-бота проектирует cp-bot, публичные посты в ленте — cp-content-plan. Use when the user works on email campaigns, newsletters, welcome or nurture sequences, reactivation, or email deliverability proble…

Supports checkpointing for pause/resume. Triggers: execute, implement, start working, run the protocol, build it, code this.

Use para mapear cenas, fala, composição, tipografia, movimento e áudio e gerar relatório, CSV, receita JSON e prompt de recriação; extração não autoriza produzir a edição.

name: cp-funnel
description: Строит карту пути «касание → вовлечение → подписка → прогрев → заявка → продажа → повтор» и находит узкое место по конверсиям между этапами, а не по абсолютным числам. Разводит воронку контента (охват → удержание → действие → подписка) и воронку продаж, чтобы их не лечили друг другом. Держит режим малых чисел: на десятках наблюдений конверсия неразличима, и скилл говорит это прямо вместо оптимизации шума. Знает реальность российского учёта — Метрика с Logs API за предыдущий день, соцсети без выгрузок, потеря источника при переходах из мессенджеров — и даёт ручные способы разметки. Отдаёт схем…

name: cp-geo
description: Работает с видимостью сайта в ответах нейросетей — Алисы AI, AI Overviews, ChatGPT — и отделяет четыре подтверждённых факта от общих рассуждений, которыми заполнены русскоязычные материалы про GEO. name: cp-geo
description: Работает с видимостью сайта в ответах нейросетей: проверяет цитируемость, структуру материалов, ИИ-краулеров и долю упоминаний. Разделяет доступные наблюдения и гипотезы, не обещает попадание в ответы. Обычный поиск и семантику ведёт cp-seo. name: cp-hook
description: Генерирует первые строки коротких видео по таксономии из шести психологических механизмов и 25 типов. Выдаёт 8–10 вариантов с разметкой (механизм, тип, аватар, счёт слов, риск отвала), затем отсеивает до двух лучших с обоснованием. Разводит хук (первая произносимая строка, 5–6 слов, 3 секунды) и вход (такт 0:00–0:06) — вход собирает cp-script-short. Умеет выдавать пары под встроенный A/B на Instagram Trial Reels. name: cp-humanizer

Живые неровности речи сохраняет: гладкий текст без швов — тоже брак. Use when a Russian text reads as AI-generated, bureaucratic, or suspiciously smooth. Отвечает за то, что написано на странице и в каком порядке; за стек, хостинг и скорость отвечает cp-web, за формулировку самого оффера и цены — cp-offer. description: Reference for building a curated drug spectral library where MS/MS spectra from public repositories must be joined to harmonized pharmacologic metadata sourced from PubChem, DrugCentral, ChEMBL, DrugBank, or the Broad Drug Repurposing Hub.

name: cross-database-entity-reconciliation
description: Use when you have chemical entity records scattered across two or more public repositories (e.g., HMDB, ChEMBL, PubChem, KEGG) and need a single authoritative, deduplicated knowledge base indexed by a queryable identifier (e.g., m/z value or chemical formula).

name: cross-database-gene-label-mapping
description: Use when you have a candidate HVG list (e.g. ~16,000 genes from FindVariableFeatures(), variance, scannpy, M3drop) and need database-derived communication-relevance labels to retain only genes involved in cell-cell communication.

name: cross-database-identifier-harmonization
description: Reference for annotating an InChIKey-keyed metabolite table with cross-database identifiers and chemical properties when datasets from different studies must be merged and compared on shared keys.

name: cross-database-identifier-mapping
description: Use when assembling a unified reaction-rule/metabolite-structure resource from separately maintained databases (e.g., RetroRules rules lacking mass shifts, LOTUS entries not in SQLite) before rule- or mass-based metabolite annotation.

name: cross-database-identifier-mapping
description: Use when integrating pathway/annotation records from HMDB XML, KEGG REST responses, Reactome ChEBI/UniProt mappings, or WikiPathways GPML files whose metabolite and gene identifiers use different, overlapping schemes.

name: cross-database-identifier-mapping-interpretation
description: Use when you have a merged/harmonized metabolite table (e.g. the 391-entry urinary asthma metabolite MMS output) and need to report or audit what percentage of entries carry each non-systematic identifier before interpreting or comparing annotations across databases.

name: cross-database-identifier-resolution
description: Use when a sparse metabolite table has known primary identifiers (e.g. HMDB IDs) but empty fields for other databases, and you need complete cross-database mapping for pathway enrichment or annotation.

name: cross-database-identifier-retrieval
description: Use when a metabolomics input table lists compounds under inconsistent names or synonyms and the rows must be keyed to unambiguous database identifiers (CID, InChIKey, KEGG, ChEBI, HMDB, DrugBank) before downstream aggregation or meta-analysis.

name: cross-database-identifier-table-population
description: Use when you need a local cross-database identifier cache for metabolomics ID mapping (HMDB, ChEBI, LIPID MAPS, KEGG, PubChem) and repeated lookups must avoid live HTTP calls to KEGG/PubChem.

name: cross-database-interaction-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have a FAVA (favapy) predicted protein-pair network with Pearson-correlation confidence scores and need to quantify how many of its high-confidence edges are novel vs. supported by STRING, hu.MAP 2.0, or the IDG Tdark catalogue.

name: cross-database-metabolomics-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a study requires searching a query MS/MS spectrum (or an entire .

name: cross-database-nomenclature-alignment
description: Use when when you have lipid abbreviations or names from different databases (HMDB, LIPID MAPS, LipidHome, RefMet, SwissLipids) or lipidomics software (LipidSearch, MS-DIAL, LipidBlast, etc.) that must be cross-referenced, compared, or integrated into a single annotation scheme.

name: cross-database-overlap-analysis
description: Use when comparing adduct or molecule inventories across multiple published databases to quantify overlap, novel additions, and exclusions via set operations on harmonized names, formulas, and monoisotopic masses.

name: cross-database-polya-site-comparison
description: Use when a set of predicted polyA sites or 3'-end bins must be benchmarked against public polyA site annotations (PolyASite, PolyA_DB) instead of a sample-specific gold standard.

name: cross-database-record-count-verification
description: Use when reproducing a data-processing pipeline from a manuscript and you need to confirm the cleaned dataset size matches the reported figure (e.g., CCSBase 16,989 → 13,617 points) before any model training.

name: cross-database-set-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify how many entries of an in-house metabolite/lipid library overlap with a public reference database, e.g., verifying claims that CMM 3.0's oxidized lipids are 'not present in other sources'.

name: cross-database-spectral-record-retrieval
description: Use when the same physical mass spectrum must be reconciled across MassBank, MoNA, GNPS, HMDB, MetaboLights, or mzCloud entries whose accession IDs differ, and a database-independent identifier is needed to confirm they refer to the same spectrum.

name: cross-database-structural-homology-matching
description: Use when when you have antiSMASH-predicted BGCs and wish to link them to metabolomic data via structure prediction, but only BGCs with sufficient structural homology to characterized reference clusters will yield reliable predictions.

name: cross-database-taxonomic-similarity-analysis
description: Use when the same OTU representative sequences have been taxonomically assigned with multiple reference databases and you need to quantify assignment concordance per taxonomic level (Phylum through Species).

name: cross-database-verification
description: Verify gap existence across multiple databases (Semantic Scholar, Google Scholar, arXiv, domain-specific). Distinguishes database-specific gaps from universal gaps.

name: cross-database-virome-overlap-analysis
description: Use when a newly assembled viral genome catalogue (e.g. 14,224 quality-filtered genomes >=50% CheckV completeness) must be dereplicated into vOTUs and its novelty estimated against existing virome reference databases.

name: cross-datacenter-clock-sync-validation
description: Use when a strategy merges ticks from more than one datacenter (NY4, LD4, a cloud region) and must prove those sites agree closely enough to order events correctly. Measures pairwise inter-region drift with its uncertainty and fails closed.

name: cross-dataset-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when replicating or validating a published benchmark (e.g., FSA rank#1/top-5 accuracy and runtime) across several MS/MS test datasets against reported numeric results.

name: cross-dataset-algorithm-comparison
description: Use when a new alignment or feature-correspondence method must be validated against established software on ≥2 benchmark datasets with ground-truth manual annotations, and per-dataset accuracy deltas are the target output.

name: cross-dataset-assembly-metric-aggregation
description: Use when comparing de novo transcriptome assembler quality across datasets whose gene-detection depth differs, and raw counts of 95%-assembled genes are not directly comparable without Kallisto-based normalization.

name: cross-dataset-barcode-precision-validation
description: Use when you need to quantify false cell barcode or UMI assignment rates for Nanopore reads, or to validate Nanopore-assigned cellBC/UMI pairs against an independent Illumina short-read dataset from the same sample.

name: cross-dataset-batch-effect-evaluation
description: Use when comparing reference-based cell-type mapping methods across two single-cell datasets with batch effect and strong asymmetry in cell number and library depth (e.g., whole-cell scRNA-seq reference to ultra-sparse snRNA-seq nuclei target).

name: cross-dataset-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a spectral/annotation method's accuracy claim must be validated across two or more independent test sets (e.g. NPLIB1 vs MassSpecGym) rather than a single benchmark.

name: cross-dataset-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing competing feature sets or representations for cell clustering across several scRNA-seq datasets, requiring replicate-level metrics (AMI) against known subpopulation labels to show consistency.

name: cross-dataset-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when validating an automatic cluster annotation method on several independent published scRNA-seq datasets with known manual annotations, to report per-dataset consistency rates and an overall average.

name: cross-dataset-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a classifier's robustness must be benchmarked across multiple independently sequenced scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., 6 cross-platform human pancreas training-test pairs), comparing 2+ annotation methods by mean classification accuracy.

name: cross-dataset-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when a target paper reports a metrics table across multiple datasets or evaluation conditions and the goal is to independently re-run the proposed method plus baselines to verify the reported ordering and values.

name: cross-dataset-bgc-cross-referencing
description: Use when mass spectrometry identifications from multiple GNPS microbial datasets can be paired with genome mining data from the same strains and you need to validate identifications or discover novel BGC-to-molecule links.

name: cross-dataset-biomarker-reproducibility-assessment
description: Use when a biomarker-discovery pipeline (e.g. CAMAMED with cumulative sum-scaling and metagenomeSeq) has produced case-control marker taxa/genes from one metagenome dataset and an independent dataset from the same study context is available to test whether the markers reproduce.

name: cross-dataset-cell-annotation-evaluation
description: Use when you have 2+ annotated scRNA-seq reference datasets with batch effects and a held-out unlabeled target dataset, and you need cross-dataset cell-type annotation plus an evaluation against known labels.

name: cross-dataset-cell-embedding-evaluation
description: Use when scRNA-seq datasets with overlapping cell types must be integrated and you need to quantify dataset mixing vs. cell-type resolution for competing correction methods (e.g., ComBat, MNN, CCA, Harmony, scVI, DIRECTi).

name: cross-dataset-cell-label-integration
description: Use when per-dataset cell subtype fine labels have been produced (fine-labels.RDS per dataset) and you need to reconcile or compare subtype label definitions across published references by constructing a cross-dataset Jaccard similarity matrix.

name: cross-dataset-cell-population-matching
description: Use when two or more annotated scRNA-seq datasets (batch-corrected/aligned, e.g. with scVI or Seurat) must have their cell population labels matched and a hierarchical classification tree learned, especially when name-based matching fails (e.g. different labs, resolutions, or nomenclatures).

name: cross-dataset-cell-type-mapping
description: Use when a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset and an unlabeled target dataset (e.g., Drop-seq reference to Smart-seq2 target, or Smart-Seq2 to CEL-Seq pancreas) must be mapped across technologies or batch conditions.

name: cross-dataset-cell-type-prediction
description: Use when a labeled training scRNA-seq dataset (h5ad) must annotate cells from a different dataset — same species or cross-species — where the test set contains cell types with no annotated cells in the training data.

name: cross-dataset-cell-type-replicability-assessment
description: Use when you need to measure whether cell types (e.g., neurons vs non-neurons, excitatory vs inhibitory, interneuron subtypes) identified in one scRNA-seq study replicate in independent studies, or to find reciprocal top-hit cell-type pairs across datasets.

name: cross-dataset-cell-type-transfer
description: Use when a pre-annotated reference scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., .h5ad from GEO) must be used to label cells in a different test dataset whose taxonomy may contain unseen cell types, and errors from noise/batch effects need suppression.

name: cross-dataset-classifier-comparison
description: Use when a new cell-annotation or classification method must be compared against established algorithms on the same ground-truth-labeled scRNA-seq test sets with ranked, per-dataset metrics.

name: cross-dataset-clustering-benchmark-aggregation
description: Use when benchmarking a clustering model across multiple scRNA-seq datasets and random seeds (e.g. 20 datasets, seeds 1111–10000) and you must assemble per-dataset mean/median ARI comparisons into one table.

name: cross-dataset-clustering-comparison
description: Use when you need to compare a scRNA-seq cell clustering method's accuracy (ARI) against published tools across many datasets with known cell type labels, e.g. benchmarking scQA on GEO/ArrayExpress data such as GSE57249 or E-MTAB-5061.

name: cross-dataset-clustering-ordering-comparison
description: Use when you have clustered spectra from ≥2 MS/MS clustering tools on ≥2 metabolomics datasets and need MS-RT purity/N10 scores to test whether tool rankings (e.g. Falcon vs MaRaCluster) transfer across instruments.

name: cross-dataset-coexpression-reproducibility-assessment
description: Use when multiple methods infer cell-type-specific co-expression from scRNA-seq data and you must test which method's significant gene pairs replicate in an independent dataset.

name: cross-dataset-component-comparability-handling
description: Use when decomposing individual tumor scRNA-seq expression matrices with ICA (n_components=100) and you need gene loading scales and orientations comparable across components and datasets before downstream clustering or pan-cancer integration.

name: cross-dataset-consistency-analysis
description: Use when differential abundance results exist for the same phenotype across multiple independent datasets (e.g., five diarrhea or five obesity studies) and you need to quantify which DA tools call the same genera significant more often than expected by chance.

name: cross-dataset-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when the goal is to identify genes consistently dysregulated across several public transcriptomics cohorts (e.g. severe vs mild COVID-19 peripheral blood RNA-seq) instead of relying on a single-dataset DE result.

name: cross-dataset-drug-response-scale-transformation
description: Use when drug response data come from datasets with incompatible units (e.g., GDSC IC50 vs PRISM Repurposing 19Q4 AUC) and must be placed on a common sensitivity scale before model training or cross-dataset correlation.

name: cross-dataset-empathy-benchmark-combination
description: Use when the goal is to reproduce or exceed the empathy prediction scores (PCC/CCC/RMSE) on the NewsEmp24 test set by training on the combined NewsEmp24+23+22 data with noise-mitigated labels.

name: cross-dataset-entry-filtering
description: Use when you have received MSBERT-preprocessed spectral data from GNPS, MoNA, or MTBLS1572 and need to ensure data integrity before training a spectral embedding model.

name: cross-dataset-expression-comparison
description: Use when validating that simulated scRNA-seq data reproduce a protocol-specific expression property (e.g., gene length bias in non-UMI data) by direct comparison against a matched experimental dataset.

name: cross-dataset-expression-correlation-mapping
description: Use when unsupervised BUSseq clusters need biological labels beyond FACS labels — e.g., verifying an intermediate CMP-MEP cluster or mapping a CLP/LMPP-like cluster to Haemopedia progenitor populations.

name: cross-dataset-feature-correspondence-mapping
description: Use when you have two or more nontargeted LCMS feature tables from the same analytical method (same column, ionization mode, and acquisition parameters) and need to identify which features in one dataset correspond to features in another.

name: cross-dataset-feature-match-audit
description: Use when two LC–MS metabolomics feature tables have already been matched (e.g., 4953 unique matches via M2S) and you must verify correctness using the subset of features annotated at MSI confidence level 2.

name: cross-dataset-feature-matching
description: Use when you have two or more feature tables in HDF5 format with detected features characterized by m/z, drift time, retention time, and intensity, and you need to match corresponding features across samples to account for systematic shifts caused by instrument variation or tuning differences.

name: cross-dataset-feature-matching
description: Use when two peak-picked, conventionally aligned untargeted LC-MS feature tables acquired under non-identical conditions (different gradients, instruments, or laboratories) must have their overlapping features identified and concatenated.

name: cross-dataset-feature-matching
description: Use when integrating two untargeted LC-MS metabolomics peak tables (e.g. MESA reference vs Rotterdam target) that share RT, m/z, and FI dimensions but were acquired in separate runs, and you need unique feature correspondence without MS/MS or annotation-level matching.

name: cross-dataset-feature-matching-evaluation
description: Use when you have completed feature matching between two LC-MS metabolomics datasets and need to quantify match correctness — e.g. via annotated feature concordance or a simulated dataset with known embedded correspondences.

name: cross-dataset-gene-classification-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to classify which of the top-2000 Seurat FindVariableFeatures() HVGs participate in cell-cell communication, and compare the classified gene counts across independent spatial transcriptomics datasets.

name: cross-dataset-gene-clustering
description: Use when a published gene signature (e.g. Bailey ADEX) may be confounded by tissue-nonspecific or non-tumor genes, and you have ≥2 independently parsed bulk RNAseq datasets to test cross-dataset reproducibility of gene groupings.

name: cross-dataset-gene-set-intersection
description: Use when building robust cancer-cell classification features by intersecting malignant-vs-non-malignant DEGs across multiple training scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., RCC, HNSCC, melanoma, LUAD, BC) rather than relying on a single dataset.

name: cross-dataset-generalization-assessment
description: Use when you have a pre-trained MS/MS spectral embedding model evaluated on one or more source datasets (GNPS, MoNA, MTBLS1572) and need to verify that it performs well on independent, high-quality curated spectral libraries to claim robustness.

name: cross-dataset-generalization-evaluation
description: Use when you need to test whether a CCS prediction model's reported accuracy transfers beyond its training dataset's chemical space, using METLIN-CCS (~27k structures) and CCSBase v1.3 (16,989 values) as train/test pairs.

name: cross-dataset-generalization-metrics-aggregation
description: Use when a trained GNN CCS predictor must be evaluated on a structurally different database than its training set (e.g. CCSBase→METLIN-CCS or METLIN-CCS→CCSBase) and per-model R2/MAE/MRE must be compiled into a cross-database comparison table.

name: cross-dataset-hic-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking per-cell informative chromatin interaction counts across single-cell Hi-C modalities, or when harmonizing published valid-pair datasets (e.g. GSM2254217, GSE174226) under identical distance and deduplication filters.

name: cross-dataset-intensity-normalization
description: Use when combining probe-level microarray intensity data from multiple GEO series (e.g. 3T3-L1 differentiation studies) where per-study platforms and processing differ and cross-study comparability is required.

name: cross-dataset-joins
description: Patterns for combining data from multiple Montréal datasets. Includes borough-based joins, proximity joins, temporal joins, and strategies for working around CKAN's single-table SQL limitation. / Stratégies pour combiner des données de plusieurs jeux de données : jointures par arrondissement, par proximité, par période, et contournement de la limitation SQL mono-table de CKAN.

name: cross-dataset-map-aggregation
description: Use when comparing two annotation scoring methods across a corpus of imaging mass spectrometry datasets and you need a single ranking-quality metric (MAP) per method per sample type, plus counts of datasets with statistically significant AP differences.

name: cross-dataset-mass-signature-pooling
description: Use when multiple replicate DESI-MSI datasets of the same tissue type (e.g., root sections) have each been processed along a linear developmental gradient and you need a pooled, de-replicated mass signature list for cross-sample clustering and variety comparison.

name: cross-dataset-masst-search
description: Use when an annotation made in one full-scan dataset (e.g. a pseudo MS/MS spectrum from NIST feces MSV000095787) must be validated or propagated by finding the top cosine match in a pool of pseudo MS/MS spectra from another dataset (e.g. IBD, PR000639).

name: cross-dataset-match-count-reporting
description: Use when an Eclipse MSAligner one-by-all alignment has been run (e.g., a reference dataset like rat plasma DS5 against comparison datasets DS6–DS9) and you must report how many of the reference features matched in all datasets, partially matched, or had no match.

name: cross-dataset-metadata-tabulation
description: Use when a collection of parsed expression datasets must be inventoried into a single annotation table with consistent columns (measurement type, sample description, n samples, n features, Used flag), e.g. to audit a compendium or reproduce a published dataset table.

name: cross-dataset-metagene-network-construction
description: Use when two ICA decompositions of different cancer transcriptomic datasets must be compared component-wise to assess reproducibility, and no one-to-one component ordering exists between them.

name: cross-dataset-method-comparison
description: Use when a choice among feature-selection (top-value) or partitioning methods for consensus clustering must be justified by large-scale empirical comparison across many datasets rather than a single example.

name: cross-dataset-model-benchmarking
description: Use when you must quantify how much a model component (e.g. predicted fingerprint input) contributes by re-running the identical generation/re-ranking pipeline with that component removed on held-out spectra from multiple reference datasets.

name: cross-dataset-model-evaluation
description: Use when a vision-language meme-detection model has been trained (or ablated) and must be benchmarked on more than one dataset with dataset-specific metrics such as ACC/AUROC for Hateful Memes and ACC/F1 for MultiOFF.

name: cross-dataset-model-generalization-assessment
description: Use when you have trained a neural network or regression model on one paired microbiome-metabolome dataset and wish to test whether it can predict metabolite abundances in an independent, externally-sourced dataset collected from different patient cohorts or study populations.

name: cross-dataset-model-generalization-testing
description: Use when a trained model artifact (e.g., scripted_m21.pth) must be evaluated on held-out BAMs from organisms/chemistry differing from its training set, to quantify generalization via AUC/F1 before deployment.

name: cross-dataset-model-transfer
description: Use when a trained scRNA-seq cell-type classifier must be transferred to a second dataset with different cells but overlapping cell-type labels, and prediction accuracy/F1 must be quantified against the target dataset's known labels.

name: cross-dataset-model-transfer-assessment
description: Use when a pre-trained model (e.g. aptardi's HBR model.hdf5) must be tested for generalizability across RNA-Seq datasets differing in tissue, organism, library preparation, or sequencing depth.

name: cross-dataset-model-transfer-evaluation
description: Use when you have candidate-feature tables (e.g. dsRID_whole.tsv) from multiple ENCODE long-read RNA-seq datasets and need to decide whether a self-trained random forest or the PacBio AD-trained transferred model performs better under 20-fold cross-validation.

name: cross-dataset-model-transfer-validation
description: Use when ML models trained on one cell-line panel (e.g. CCLE) have produced top features, and you need to confirm those features generalize by measuring their importance in independent datasets such as NCI60 or single-cell data.

name: cross-dataset-molecule-deduplication
description: Use when building a screening library from multiple structure databases (SDF/gzipped SDF) and non-organic, ionic, or duplicate molecules must be removed before spectrum prediction or other downstream chemistry.

name: cross-dataset-molecule-matching
description: Use when predicted RTs from one chromatographic method must be made comparable to RTs measured under independent experimental reverse-phase methods, and per-method projection errors (e.g. median absolute error in seconds) must be quantified.

name: cross-dataset-ms-alignment-benchmarking
description: Use when you must reproduce or extend a head-to-head comparison of LC-MS alignment tools (e.g. metabCombiner vs Eclipse) on multiple same-method datasets and report overlap and spurious-match counts.

name: cross-dataset-network-consistency-analysis
description: Use when you have several bulk transcriptomic cohorts with matched survival data (e.g., metastatic melanoma datasets like TCGA SKCM06) and need to test whether inferred cell-cell interaction networks are reproducible across cohorts and across different cell-type marker annotations.

name: cross-dataset-node-importance-comparison
description: Use when you have scBONITA rule-inference node importance scores for KEGG pathway networks from one or more scRNA-seq datasets and need to check whether importance scores carry context-dependent signaling information beyond topology alone.

name: cross-dataset-overlap-analysis
description: Use when a list of candidate microbial MS/MS spectra (.mgf from MZmine/GNPS networking) must be cross-validated against an independent public dataset with treatment-vs-control metadata to test biological exclusivity.

name: cross-dataset-overlapping-gene-selection
description: Use when a reference dataset (e.g. annotated HuBMAP data such as HBMP3-spleen-CC3) is being used to transfer labels to a query dataset (e.g. HBMP2-spleen-2) whose AnnData object has a different gene set, or when comparing clusterings across the two objects.

name: cross-dataset-peak-intensity-correlation
description: Use when reanalyzing publicly deposited MRM mzML raw data to verify that an automatic peak-integration pipeline reproduces previously reported, manually reviewed peak intensities on a per-metabolite basis.

name: cross-dataset-peak-overlap-analysis
description: Use when multiple peak files from different epigenomic assays (e.g. CUT&Tag, CUT&Run, ChIP-seq BED/narrowPeak) must be benchmarked against a reference for QC, overlap statistics, and functional annotation.

name: cross-dataset-peak-recovery-assessment
description: Use when replicating or validating an MSI peak-identification pipeline against a published peak list (e.g., the 63 peaks of Zhang et al. 2023) using multiple replicate DESI-MSI datasets.

name: cross-dataset-performance-delta-tabulation
description: Use when a paper reports a multi-dataset ablation grid (e.g., CoT chain counts n and per-perspective chains m) and you need to compute ablated-minus-full metric deltas (ACC, AUROC, F1) per dataset and visualize them.

name: cross-dataset-promoter-comparison
description: Use when two or more transcription start site (TSS) datasets for the same organism must be benchmarked against each other, and a motif-positioning-based quality comparison of nascent vs. annotated TSSs is desired.

name: cross-dataset-provenance-merging
description: Use when metabolite entries from datasets being merged carry non-systematic identifiers (CAS, HMDB, KEGG, PubChem, ChEBI, LipidMaps, DrugBank, Bin ID) that must be converted to InChIKeys before datasets can be integrated.

name: cross-dataset-read-depth-normalization
description: Use when circRNA BSJ or isoform counts must be compared across independent datasets (e.g., isoCirc nanopore libraries vs. short-read RNA-seq) generated at different sequencing depths over multiple tissues.

name: cross-dataset-read-length-stability-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether an RNA-seq expression quantification parameter is robust to sequencing length or strategy differences, by building virtual short-read/single-end derivatives from paired-end data and comparing median quantification values.

name: cross-dataset-reference-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when cell type-specific genomic features (loops, peaks, enhancers) from one dataset must be validated against independent cell type-matched epigenomic or transcriptomic reference datasets.

name: cross-dataset-reference-evaluation
description: Use when you need to evaluate or tune a reference-based cell-type identifier (e.g. MarkerCount_Ref) without holding out a dedicated training set, by rotating multiple annotated scRNA-seq datasets through test/reference roles.

name: cross-dataset-reproducibility-analysis
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq h5ad files annotated with adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta'] from a DeepCycle run and need to verify cell cycle annotation or the RNA-doubling prior by quantifying UMI-vs-phase fold change across multiple cell systems.

description: Use when when you have applied multiple scoring functions (e.g., strain correlation and IOKR) to rank genomic-metabolomic (GCF-MF or BGC-spectrum) links and need to verify that: (1) standardisation produces zero mean and unit variance across all links;

name: cross-dataset-shared-gene-merging
description: Use when two or more scRNA-seq AnnData objects with partially non-overlapping (or homologous but differently ordered) gene lists must be merged into a single cells-by-genes matrix before integration, transfer, or runtime benchmarking.

name: cross-dataset-single-cell-embedding-comparison
description: Use when the goal is to test whether predicted cell-type annotation scores (cell-by-Cell-Ontology-type matrix from OnClass Predict) integrate multiple heterogeneous scRNA-seq datasets better than expression-space integration (Scanorama), quantified by silhouette coefficient.

name: cross-dataset-spectral-comparison
description: Use when you hold MGF peak lists (with precursor m/z) from two LC-MS/MS datasets and want to compare spectral similarity versus precursor m/z difference pre-database-search, e.g. human vs. chimpanzee or human vs. E. coli serum.

name: cross-dataset-spectral-match-aggregation
description: Use when you have KGMN-annotated unknown metabolites (e.g., from Demo_MetDNA2_NIST_urine_pos) and need to test whether their MS/MS spectra recur across public GNPS/MassIVE data sets as independent evidence for annotations lacking chemical standards.

name: cross-dataset-subpopulation-separation-analysis
description: Use when comparing dimension-reduction/visualization methods for temporal scRNA-seq data on their ability to resolve subpopulations within the final time point, using dip-test multimodality scores across multiple datasets.

name: cross-dataset-subtype-similarity-mapping
description: Use when you need to compare/relate cell subtype label schemes across published TME scRNA-seq references, or to cross-validate a subtype annotation model and report fold-wise accuracy and kappa within each dataset.

name: cross-dataset-taxonomic-coverage-comparison
description: Use when a study claims a new reference/training set improves on a predecessor, and the improvement must be verified by comparing taxonomic breadth (unique genera/taxa) and reference sequence counts parsed from the sets' taxonomy and FASTA files.

name: cross-dataset-tf-binding-transfer-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating cross-platform transfer of a TF binding affinity model — train on HT-SELEX per-cycle enrichment data, test on uPBM affinities, and benchmark Pearson correlation against DeepBind, BEESEM, and BindSpace.

name: cross-dataset-tf-set-intersection-analysis
description: Use when two FateCompass differential motif activity results exist for orthologous cell fates (e.g., beta cells) in distinct species or systems, and you need to compute the intersection fraction and label species-specific TF groupings.

name: cross-dataset-training-set-size-analysis
description: Use when you must justify a database's suitability as an ML training resource by comparing its labelled instance count against the training-set sizes of existing predictors in the same domain.

name: cross-dataset-validation-of-tr-identification
description: Use when a ranked TR list (e.g., BIT scores/ranks from TCGA cancer-type accessible regions) must be independently validated by asking whether top-ranked TRs are essential upon CRISPR/Cas9 knockout in the same cancer lineages (DepMap Chronos).

name: cross-dataset-weight-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing between raw-CT optimization and external-dataset (e.g. TCGA) weight optimization when only ~20–30 qPCR samples and a few internal controls are available.

name: cross-decomposition-correlation-analysis

description: Use when comparing whether a trajectory-based scRNA-seq DEG method identifies a higher fraction of literature-verified genes among its top-ranked DEGs than a competing method on the same preprocessed expression matrix.

name: cross-method-gene-ranking-comparison
description: Use when you have a spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g. 10x Visium or HDST h5ad with 2D spatial coordinates) and need to compare which top-scoring spatially variable genes one method detects that another misses.

name: cross-method-gene-set-benchmarking
description: Use when you have a ground-truth scRNA-seq dataset with known trait-relevant cells and want to test whether one method's prioritized gene set improves a second scorer (e.g., scDRS) relative to a baseline gene set (e.g., MAGMA-derived).

name: cross-method-gep-comparison
description: Use when you need to compare activity GEPs from a baseline method (e.g., cNMF at k=137 factors on MCA) with SingleCellGGM GEPs to assess cell-type specificity and shared-program recovery.

name: cross-method-grn-comparison-analysis
description: Use when evaluating a GRN inference method on time-stamped cross-sectional single-cell data against competitors (e.g., SINCERITIES, SCODE, SCRIBE, SINGE) using early-precision curves.

name: cross-method-imputation-benchmarking
description: Use when a new or existing scRNA-seq imputation method must be quantitatively compared against competing imputers by masking known non-zero values and measuring recovery error (RMSE/MAE/NMSE).

name: cross-method-integration-benchmarking
description: Use when two scRNA-seq batches must be integrated and several correction tools should be compared quantitatively on the same inputs using iLISI (batch mixing) and 50-RNN (local structure retention) against an uncorrected Original baseline.

name: cross-method-integration-evaluation
description: Use when a multi-batch scRNA-seq dataset with known ground-truth cell labels (e.g., GSE118767 sc_mixology) must be integrated and clustered by several competing methods and their accuracies compared via ARI.

name: cross-method-integration-score-aggregation
description: Use when comparing >=2 cell-type annotation or integration methods across multiple scRNA-seq datasets and you need standardized per-method metrics plus a statistical verdict (paired t-tests, p < 0.05).

name: cross-method-local-structure-preservation-comparison
description: Use when comparing batch-correction/integration methods on scRNA-seq data and you need a quantitative measure of local structure preservation (e.g., before adopting an integration method for a two-dataset comparison).

name: cross-method-loop-set-overlap-analysis
description: Use when comparing loop sets from a supervised predictor (Peakachu) with enrichment-based callers (HiCCUPS, Fit-Hi-C) on the same Hi-C matrix, to quantify overlap and orthogonal validation.

name: cross-method-macro-f1-comparison
description: Use when comparing discriminative power of marker-selection methods on scRNA-seq phenotype classification: you need each selector's features (e.g., 42 genes on IPF) scored identically via logistic regression macro-F1.

name: cross-method-mapped-read-count-comparison
description: Use when evaluating a SPLiT-seq preprocessing method against the original barcode-filtering method by comparing STAR uniquely-mapped read counts across the five SPLiT-seq samples (SAMN08567259-64, mm10/hg19).

name: cross-method-methylation-comparison
description: Use when validating a new methylation-calling method against established platforms (WGBS, EMseq, nanopolish) by comparing overall CpG methylation rates and CpG coverage per sample.

name: cross-method-metric-normalization
description: Use when a paper reports results under one metric (e.g. LLM-as-a-Judge accuracy/precision) while baselines report incompatible metrics (Hit@1, F1) on different dataset samples and a comparison table must be built honestly.

name: cross-method-model-comparison
description: Use when a new classifier (e.g. Pollock) must be evaluated head-to-head against multiple established methods on identical annotated single-cell datasets with predefined train/validation splits, using F1 as the comparison metric.

name: cross-method-module-count-comparison
description: Use when comparing module granularity of co-expression methods (SGCRNA vs WGCNA/hdWGCNA) on the same gene or genus-level count matrix, e.g. bulk RNA-Seq, Visium spatial, or 16S amplicon data.

name: cross-method-network-comparison
description: Use when you need to validate a network inference tool against a baseline method on the same time-series dataset, comparing recovery of literature/ChIP-derived regulons against random regulator profiles.

name: cross-method-network-comparison
description: Use when several co-occurrence networks (e.g., SparCC, propr, SpiecEasi, FlashWeave, COZINE, HARMONIES, SPRING, mLDM) have been inferred from the same abundance table and you need to quantify shared vs. unique nodes/edges to reveal method-driven rewiring.

name: cross-method-network-comparison
description: Use when evaluating a gene co-expression network inference method against alternatives on scRNA-seq data and you need quantitative computational-efficiency and robustness comparisons rather than only accuracy metrics.

name: cross-method-network-consistency-evaluation
description: Use when true gene networks are unknown for real single-cell data and inferred TF–gene edges must be validated against ChIP-seq references, comparing scLink with PIDC, Pearson, Spearman, and glasso variants per cell type.

name: cross-method-normalisation-comparison
description: Use when a large-scale metabolomics dataset (e.g. >1,000 plasma samples acquired over 44 days on an Agilent 1260 HPLC/Qtrap5500 platform) has been normalised by two or more competing methods and you need an empirical, replicate-based comparison of which removes unwanted variation while preserving.

name: cross-method-pas-scoring-comparison
description: Use when PAS must be computed on large-scale scRNA-seq data (>10^3 pathways, up to million-cell atlases) and an original vs. accelerated implementation comparison is needed.

name: cross-method-pathway-concordance-analysis
description: Use when a large-scale scRNA-seq study requires validating that a fast pathway-activity method (scPAFA/fast_Ucell) detects the same disease-related differential pathways as a slower reference (SCPA), while quantifying compute cost.

name: cross-method-pathway-rank-comparison
description: Use when a labeled RNA-seq expression matrix must be benchmarked across sample-wise pathway quantification methods to rank a target pathway (e.g., TNFa signaling in IL17+TNFa-treated vs control samples) by significance.

name: cross-method-pathway-ranking-comparison
description: Use when a single-cell differential comparison (e.g., stimulated vs control PBMCs) has been scored for pathway/gene-module activity by both a Bayes Factor test (VEGA) and a ranked-list enrichment method (GSEA) and the goal is a side-by-side significance comparison.

name: cross-method-performance-comparison
description: Use when a Source Data supplementary table must be re-analyzed to verify reported average accuracies across competing celltyping methods, e.g. the 7-task FACS-sorted PBMC targets in Fig 3a.

name: cross-method-performance-comparison
description: Use when comparing the computational cost (peak memory and total runtime) of unsupervised single-cell manifold alignment methods such as scTopoGAN, UnionCom, MMD-MA, and SCOT on one or more pre-processed single-modality datasets.

name: cross-method-performance-table-assembly
description: Use when multiple scRNA-seq clustering methods (e.g., scDCC, CIDR, DCA+k-means, DEC, MPSSC, PCA+k-means, SIMLR, SC3, Seurat) have been run on the same labeled datasets and their per-method metric values must be tabulated for comparison.

name: cross-method-prediction-overlap-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking ligand-receptor inference tools on the same scRNA-seq dataset, e.g. comparing CellChat vs CellPhoneDB/SingleCellSignalR/iTALK predictions, overlap, or robustness to cell subsampling.

name: cross-method-quantification-agreement-analysis
description: Use when the same set of peptide groups (e.g. 22 H3 groups spanning 0-3 acetyl and 0-9 methyl PTM equivalents) has been quantified by two or more label-free approaches and you need per-group agreement against a reference quantification.

name: cross-method-quantification-benchmarking
description: Use when an organism has a reference genome/transcriptome (e.g., zebrafish GRCz11, Homarus americanus GMGI_Hamer_2.0) and you must validate that Seq2Fun ortholog-based quantification reproduces Kallisto-based results.

name: cross-method-rare-cell-detection-comparison
description: Use when comparing rare cell-type detection accuracy across methods on scRNA-seq data, e.g. testing sensitivity to the number of DE genes distinguishing a rare population, or reproducing reported rare clusters in the 68k PBMC dataset.

name: cross-method-retrieval-performance-comparison
description: Use when a small-molecule NMR structure-search system (e.g. a neural fingerprint predictor) must be benchmarked against spectral-library shift-matching baselines on the same query spectra and ground-truth structures.

name: cross-method-rt-calibration
description: Use when when you have predicted retention times from a DNN model trained on one chromatographic method (CM) and need to rank or filter metabolite candidates on a different chromatographic method, but have only a small set of calibration molecules (≥10) with known RTs on both source and target.

name: cross-method-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when two normalization methods must be compared on identical data and the claim of interest is computational efficiency, e.g. timing UniFORM's automatic feature-level pipeline against MxNorm's B-spline registration on the same PRAD-CyCIF feature table.

name: cross-method-runtime-comparison
description: Use when a study must rank GRN-inference algorithms fairly on one dataset — e.g., AUROC/AUPRC vs. a reference network plus per-method runtime on identical hardware.

name: cross-method-runtime-memory-benchmarking
description: Use when two or more gene co-expression network inference methods must be compared on the same single-cell expression matrix, with runtime/memory and downstream module quality (GEP counts, GO enrichment) as head-to-head metrics.

name: cross-method-scrnaseq-mapping-comparison
description: Use when several single-cell reference-mapping methods must be compared head-to-head on the same reference/query dataset pairs, e.g. to judge whether a new mapper (ProjectSVR) matches Seurat, scArches, Symphony, ProjecTILs, iNMF or SCALEX.

name: cross-method-search-result-comparison
description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking tandem MS database search methods: you have query MS/MS spectra, a spectral library, a molecular structure database (DNP or MoNA), and need top-k accuracy comparisons across multiple search tools.

name: cross-method-speed-comparison
description: Use when comparing the computational efficiency of scDist, Augur, and nDEG on the same scRNA-seq data — full datasets, subsamples of varying size, or large simulated cohorts (~1M cells) — to record timing ratios.

name: cross-method-speed-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify and compare prediction runtime of automatic cell-type identification methods on scRNA-seq data, especially to assess how runtime scales with training/testing set size or to select a fast method for large prediction tasks.

name: cross-method-stability-scoring
description: Use when two HVG-selection or gene-classification methods (e.g. CPPLS-MLP and CCPLS) must be compared for selection stability on spatial/single-cell datasets with cell-type clusters, and per-cell-type Y HVG lists are available.

name: cross-method-svg-rank-comparison
description: Use when you need to compare the agreement of two or more spatially variable gene detection methods on identical spatial transcriptomics data, or to verify whether a method under-ranks genes with strong spatial expression patterns.

name: cross-method-top5-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how robust competing molecular-formula identification methods are to increasing spectral noise, on matched MGF test spectra from Q-TOF or Orbitrap instruments.

name: cross-method-trajectory-comparison
description: Use when a simulated dataset with known pseudotime and branching structure is available and you need to quantify which TI method assigns cells to branches most purely and reconstructs pseudotime most accurately.

name: cross-method-trajectory-comparison
description: Use when comparing RNA velocity methods on spliced/unspliced AnnData from complex differentiation scenarios (cell cycles, sparse cell types, multi-branch lineages) to decide which tool's trajectory matches expected biology.

name: cross-method-trajectory-comparison
description: Use when a single-cell pseudotime/branching result from one method (e.g., DTFLOW RSKG) needs to be validated or contextualized against branch assignments from alternative tools such as Scanpy or Monocle2.

name: cross-method-transcript-classifier-comparison
description: Use when you need to reproduce or extend head-to-head evaluation of lncRNA coding-potential classifiers on sORF-enriched test sets, computing PRE, SEN, SPE, ACC, F1, MCC, and AUC per species.

name: cross-method-twas-result-comparison
description: Use when two TWAS frameworks have been run on identical reference (e.g., GTEx V8 whole blood, n=574) and GWAS data and you must count independently significant genes per method and their overlap.

name: cross-method-velocity-metric-computation
description: Use when benchmarking two or more RNA velocity methods on the same dataset and you need comparable per-gene metrics (e.g., phase-portrait fitting quality, directional coherence) restricted to commonly modeled genes.

name: cross-metric-benchmark-comparison-scrna-seq
description: Use when you must decide which similarity metric (posterior distance vs. Euclidean) better distinguishes same-type nearest neighbors between query and reference scRNA-seq cells within a fixed embedding space.

name: cross-metric-droplet-alignment
description: Use when you have per-droplet DIEM debris scores from an snRNA-seq run and a per-droplet contamination proxy (e.g., percent spliced reads) and need to verify the debris score tracks extranuclear RNA contamination.

name: cross-mfe-contract
description: Cria ou altera um evento compartilhado ou a tabela de rotas em packages/contracts. Use quando dois apps precisam se comunicar, quando um evento existente muda de formato, ou quando uma rota é adicionada ou renomeada.

name: cross-mod
description: Hub for building plugins that run in both Claude Code and Google Antigravity (agy) with the Bifrost framework. Use when starting any plugin work under plugins/<mod> to find the right specialized skill and the end-to-end workflow, including when the plugin seems to need something Bifrost lacks.

name: cross-mod
description: Hub for building plugins that run in both Claude Code and Google Antigravity (agy) with the Bifrost framework. Use when starting any plugin work in this repository to find the right specialized skill and the end-to-end workflow.

name: cross-mod-testing
description: Testing Bifrost plugins - Bun tests with the @gidragir/bifrost/testing kit, engine tests run by claude plugin test against the built plugin, type checking and Biome. Use when writing or running tests, debugging a failing check, or deciding which layer a test belongs to.

name: cross-modal-alignment-training
description: Use when after completing pretraining and fine-tuning stages when you have a checkpoint with task-specific performance but need to improve cross-modal consistency.

name: cross-modal-attention-fusion
description: Use when fine-grained visual-textual alignment is needed for meme or vision-language classification, especially when standard CLIP encoders fail on long CoT texts (>20 tokens, ~150-word sequences).

name: cross-modal-community-composition-analysis
description: Use when an anchor network of molecular programs has been integrated across datasets/modalities (e.g. from a thresholded Pearson correlation matrix) and you need its community partition and the modality composition of each community.

name: cross-modal-convergence
description: Cross-modal representational convergence methodology using Generalized Procrustes Algorithm to measure intra-modal dispersion at single-stimulus level. Low intra-modal dispersion predicts up to 2× higher cross-modal alignment. Activation: representational similarity, RSA, Procrustes, cross-modal, model-brain alignment, vision-language, DINOv2.

name: cross-modal-convergence-dispersion
description: Measuring cross-modal neural network convergence using single-stimulus intra-modal dispersion. Generalized Procrustes Algorithm for quantifying how stimuli with low intra-modal dispersion elicit higher cross-modal alignment. Activation triggers: cross-modal convergence, neural network alignment, vision-language alignment, representational similarity.

name: cross-modal-convergence-modulation
description: Modulating Cross-Modal Convergence with Single-Stimulus, Intra-Modal Dispersion - neural network methodology for modulating representational convergence across architectures and modalities. Reveals how single-stimulus dispersion within modalities predicts cross-modal alignment. Based on arXiv:2604.21836.

name: cross-modal-decoder-generation
description: Use when a trained scMM model's latent dimensions need interpretation: sweep each latent dimension independently through the mixture-of-experts decoder to link genes, surface proteins, and chromatin accessibility peaks to individual dimensions.

name: cross-modal-dispersion-convergence
description: Cross-modal convergence analysis methodology using Generalized Procrustes Algorithm to measure intra-modal representational convergence at single-stimulus level. Reveals how low intra-modal dispersion (high agreement among vision models) elicits significantly higher cross-modal alignment between vision and language models. Activation: cross-modal convergence, representational alignment, Procrustes analysis, vision-language alignment, neural representation, single-stimulus analysis

name: cross-modal-gan-domain-mapping
description: Use when two separately measured single-cell modalities of related cells must be aligned or a missing modality predicted — e.g., spatial transcriptomics to scRNA-seq or paired ATAC-seq/RNA-seq — while preserving data geometry.

name: cross-modal-gene-list-comparison
description: Use when a target gene's correlated-gene ranking from original spatial data must be compared against the same ranking computed on a GAN-mapped scRNA-seq output to flag spurious vs. newly discovered candidate associations.

name: cross-modal-generation
description: Guides InternGPT ImageBind/StableUnCLIP audio, thermal, image, text generation and StyleGAN/DragGAN point editing workflows.

name: cross-modal-generation
description: Master skill for generating content across modalities. Covers text-to-image, image-to-text, audio-to-visual, cross-modal translation, multimodal fusion, style transfer, and content synthesis.

name: cross-modal-hybrid-denoising-pretraining
description: Use when pretraining a sequence-to-sequence model on a corpus of fingerprint–SELFIES pairs (e.g. 4M PubChem molecules) to teach cross-modal mapping between Morgan fingerprint tokens and molecular structures before finetuning on spectra.

name: cross-modal-normalization
description: Scale alignment for RNA-protein cross-modal integration - BOTH modalities must be z-scored

name: cross-modal-protein-generation-from-transcriptome
description: Use when you have paired CITE-seq transcriptome and surface protein counts (RNA_count.mtx/gene.tsv and Protein_count.mtx/protein.tsv with barcode.tsv) and need to predict protein measurements for cells whose protein data is withheld, given transcriptome observations alone.

name: cross-modal-review
description: Quality gate via second model. Spawn a different AI model to review work before committing. Includes refusal routing: if one model refuses, switch silently to the next. Extended in v0.25.1 with structured review-mode gating (when to invoke vs not) and a Codex code-review handoff for the diff-review case.

name: cross-modal-review
description: Quality gate via a second AI model. Spawn a different model to review work before committing. Grades against the originating skill's Contract. Use when you want a second opinion from a different model, or the user says "second opinion", "cross-modal review", "double check this", or "get another perspective".

name: cross-modal-review
description: Quality gate via second model. Spawn a different AI model to review work before committing. Includes refusal routing: if one model refuses, switch silently to the next. Extended in v1.1 with structured review-mode gating (when to invoke vs not) and a second-model code-review handoff for the diff-review case.

name: cross-modal-review
description: Quality gate via second model. Spawn a different AI model to review work before committing. Includes refusal routing: if one model refuses, silently switch to the next.

name: cross-modal-review
description: Run a second-model quality gate on staged changes, a skill draft, or any generated output. A cheaper, independent model reviews the primary output for correctness, safety, and completeness before the user sees the final result.

name: cross-modal-review
description: Évalue la qualité d'un MEMORY.md de subject (Quick + Détails régénérés par /documente) en faisant noter par 2-3 modèles distincts (Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5) sur 4 axes : cohérence, complétude, spécificité, citations. Adapté du pattern "cross-modal eval" de Garry Tan (cf. analyse Forge-Lab 2026-05-09). Trigger sur "review ce subject", "evaluate ce MEMORY", "cross-modal eval", "score la synthèse".

name: cross-modal-review
description: Quality gate via second model. Spawn a different AI model to review work before committing. A refusal is reported to the user as a provider refusal, never hidden. Extended in v0.25.1 with structured review-mode gating (when to invoke vs not) and a Codex code-review handoff for the diff-review case.

name: cross-modal-rna-protein-correlation-benchmarking
description: Use when paired scRNA-seq/ADT data are available and you must quantify whether a prediction (or RNA signal itself) tracks measured protein levels cell-by-cell — e.g. comparing imputation methods or raw/denoised RNA baselines per protein.

name: cross-modal-sensory-brand-congruence
description: Apply multisensory and cross-modal congruence principles to make brand experiences more memorable, trustworthy, and emotionally resonant. Covers visual-auditory-tactile alignment, sensory consistency rules, and the neuroscience of cross-modal memory enhancement. Use when designing brand identity systems, campaign creative, product packaging, or digital experiences that must stick in memory. NOT for single-channel tactical execution without sensory coordination.

name: cross-modal-similarity-validation
description: Use when you need to check that structurally-derived relationships (ontology graph distances) are recapitulated by an independent data modality (gene expression or text embeddings) before trusting the structure for downstream inference.

name: cross-modal-skill
description: This skill allows the agent to search the web using an LLM.

name: cross-modal-vision
description: Multimodal visual inspection, UI layout debugging, screenshot analysis, and visual regression testing using meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct. Activate when inspecting screenshots, verifying frontend layouts, or analyzing images.

name: cross-modality-alignment-robustness-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify how robust a cross-modality alignment (e.g. scATAC-to-scRNA via scTopoGAN) is to cell-number imbalance, by generating downsamples from 90% to 10% of cells and measuring alignment quality per fraction.

name: cross-modality-benchmark-table-generation
description: Use when each single-cell modality (e.g., PBMC RNA/ATAC, BM RNA/ADT) must be projected to a low-dimensional latent by multiple methods and compared in one table of KL0.01/KL0.1/KL1 and Silhouette metrics.

name: cross-modality-cell-assignment-agreement-evaluation
description: Use when a joint single-cell assay (e.g. sci-L3-RNA/ATAC) yields count matrices per modality plus per-cell SNV genotype calls, and you must quantify whether each modality alone distinguishes cell types correctly.

name: cross-modality-cell-pairing
description: Use when single-nucleus RNA and ATAC data from the same tissue were captured in separate assays (no shared barcodes) and downstream pseudotime or eGRN analysis needs each ATAC cell paired to an RNA cell.

name: cross-modality-common-gene-selection
description: Use when preparing unpaired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq inputs for scBridge: the target gene activity matrix and the source count matrix must be reduced to their common gene set before encoding.

name: cross-modality-correlation-metric-computation
description: Use when two modalities are jointly measured (e.g. DBIT-seq spatial transcriptomics and proteomics) and you must score whether a learned cross-domain mapping preserves point-wise correspondence, not just distributional similarity.

name: cross-modality-cost-matrix-construction
description: Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities (e.g. scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq or surface protein counts) that share only a weak, partial set of features, and a cell-level coupling cost is needed for Optimal Transport-based alignment.

name: cross-modality-embedding-integration
description: Use when you have paired scATAC-seq peak matrices and scRNA-seq gene expression matrices from the same cells (multiome data) and need to perform joint clustering, visualization, or correlation analysis across both chromatin accessibility and gene expression in a single coordinate system.

name: cross-modality-encoder-input-preparation
description: Use when a raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix (AnnData, rows=cells, columns=peaks) must be converted into a VAE-compatible, [0,1]-scaled matrix before feeding a cross-modality translation model's ATAC encoder.

name: cross-modality-feature-connection-computation
description: Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities (e.g. scRNA-seq with smFISH or scATAC-seq) where features are only weakly connected across modalities and a feature-level cost matrix is needed for rIOT-based alignment.

name: cross-modality-image-registration-evaluation
description: Use when paired multi-modal images (e.g., TOF-SIMS metabolite and IMC protein channels) need alignment and you must quantitatively verify that a registration method beats simpler baselines.

name: cross-modality-label-matching-evaluation
description: Use when you have aligned source/target single-cell latent manifolds (e.g. ATAC projected onto RNA space by scTopoGAN) plus cell type labels, and need a metric of alignment quality or a stability check across random GAN initializations.

name: cross-modality-marker-enrichment-testing
description: Use when after multi-omic integration you have reclustered cells (e.g. B cells and monocytes at Louvain resolution 0.2) and need statistical evidence that subcluster markers are shared across modalities (scRNA vs scATAC) rather than an alignment artifact.

name: cross-modality-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a single-modality dataset (e.g., scATAC-seq from BMMC batches) must be translated consecutively to a downstream modality (ADT via CITE_BMMC) and compared head-to-head with alternative translator pipelines under a labeled ground truth.

name: cross-modality-program-usage-integration
description: Use when per-patient program/community usage values exist in ≥2 -omics modalities (e.g., RNA and protein in CPTAC GBM) and the goal is to test whether combined cross-modality usage reveals clinical (survival) associations.

name: cross-modality-pseudo-count-generation
description: Use when a mosaic multi-omics dataset (e.g. CITE-seq + ASAP-seq batches) has batch–modality slots with no count matrix and you need pseudo-counts for those slots before running scMoMaT first-stage training.

name: cross-modality-roi-assignment-handling
description: Use when joint protein-metabolite single-cell analysis in crowded human tissues requires correctly registered IMC and SIMS modalities per imaging region, e.g. before computing neighbor-based metabolite competition ratios or distance-to-vessel maps.

name: cross-modality-scatac-seq-annotation
description: Use when the target data are single-cell multi-omic counts (10x Genomics PBMC CITE-seq with antibody-derived tags, or scATAC-seq such as mouse bone marrow) and only pre-trained scEMAIL source weights (encoder h, classifier c, auxiliary c1/c2) are available.

name: cross-modality-segmentation-transfer
description: Use when a segmentation pipeline validated on one multiplexed imaging modality (e.g., MIBI, IMC, imaging mass cytometry) must be evaluated on another platform or marker set to demonstrate cross-tissue/platform transferability.

name: cross-modality-shared-gene-subsetting
description: Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities (e.g. scRNA-seq with scATAC, smFISH, or surface protein/CyTOF data) whose native features differ, so modality-specific features must be converted to gene-level common features to compute a cross-modality cell distance for Optimal Transport.

name: cross-modality-single-cell-cluster-label-consistency
description: Use when you have one scRNA-seq and one scATAC-seq sample from the same heterogeneous population and need linked subpopulations with identical cluster labels across both modalities before comparative gene regulatory analysis.

name: cross-modality-translation-model-training
description: Use when paired single-cell count matrices (e.g., scRNA-seq genes and scATAC-seq peaks as AnnData) are available and a held-out single-modality profile must be translated into the other modality while preserving cellular heterogeneity.

name: cross-modality-translation-scrna-scatac
description: Use when paired or unpaired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data are available and ATAC-only profiles must be converted to RNA-like profiles, e.g., to annotate scATAC-seq cell types via translated RNA expression.

name: cross-mode-annotation-verification
description: Decision support for consolidating LC/MS feature annotations when the same extract was analyzed in both positive and negative ion mode and you need to verify which quasi-molecular ion (e.g. [M+H]+ vs [M-H]−) each grouped compound spectrum really represents.

name: cross-model
description: Consult a different model for orthogonal reasoning on a consequential decision, especially when confident. Discovers whichever model CLI is installed rather than assuming a vendor. Use when the user says "second opinion", "cross-model", "ask another model", "stress-test this", "what am I missing", "red-team this decision", or before committing to an architecture, a schema, a security boundary, or anything hard to reverse. For a reversible local decision or routine implementation, proceed directly; for a question with one verifiable answer, read the source instead.

name: cross-model
description: Get an independent review from the other model family for a plan, branch diff, or adversarial failure analysis. Use when requested and whenever root guidance requires cross-model review for work larger than a small bug fix.

name: cross-model-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing several LLMs' outputs against quantitative user-specified targets (e.g., calories) and you need per-model MAE/MAE % metrics to rank adherence, as in reproducing Table II of the NutriGen paper.

name: cross-model-advisor
description: Consults a strong different-family model as a peer reasoning partner to pair-reason and hunt blind spots (the project's binding may name it — e.g. "the Codex Advisor"). Advisory only: positions and confidence, never severity-rated findings. Use on load-bearing decisions, roadblocks, presumed-mandatory whenever the main loop is running below the project's frontier tier, and ALWAYS on "reason deeply" / "think deeply" / "/advisor". Not audit-cycle or council.

name: cross-model-audit
description: Use after one AI (for example Codex, used when Claude tokens ran out) made significant changes, to have a different model audit the work.

name: cross-model-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when several trained synthesis/generation models must be compared on identical test data with quantitative image-quality metrics to establish which architecture outperforms the baselines.

name: cross-model-benchmark-comparison

name: cross-review

name: cross-review

Use at the review stage of every code change, sized to the job (one reviewer for a small change, a three-reviewer panel for a big one), for a plan or prose package its repository sends to review, after a fix batch (resume where supported), or when the user asks for a second opinion / "ask codex…

name: cross-review
description: Request an independent Codex, Claude Code or Antigravity audit of research or code through the capsule review runtime, choose reviewer models, answer reviewer questions, and address findings. Use when cross-agent review is requested or part of an agreed research workflow.

name: cross-review

Use when the user wants "a second opinion", "have codex review this", cross-model review before merge, or when stakes justify two independent reviewers.

name: cross-review

name: cross-review

Read-only review by the other model family (Codex when Claude wrote the work, Claude when Codex did) of a committed change or a draft document, plus triage of hosted review findings: scope and materiality, dispositions kept in a review ledger, related-instance searches, convergence and verified convention learning. Returns the reviewed SHA or digest, coverage, dispositions, unresolved blockers and where the evidence is.

name: cross-review
description: 差分を 2 観点で独立レビューするときに使う。指摘の報告まで。

name: cross-review

Use when the user asks Codex or Claude to review code, wants a second opinion from another agent or model, wants a re-review that does not repeat rejected findings, or manages a running cross-review. name: cross-review

Works from any agent; the panel runs in OpenCode.

name: cross-review

Used by requirements-engineer before PRD handoff, inside QA for its required evidence review, and after creating a concept, architecture, wave plans, or P7 curated docs. Works before P0 without state.json. Not a replacement for runtime QA or form/size caps.

name: cross-review

Use when you have committed a change that is ready to ship and the repo expects review before a PR is marked ready or merged; also for a follow-up review of fixes, which covers only the commits since the last review. Decides whether a review is worth running, when to launch it, and how to act on findings.

name: cross-review
description: 別モデル視点で実装をレビューする。CLAUDE_CROSS_REVIEW=1 のとき evaluator 前に必須。「クロスレビューして」でも使う。

Runs inline in the main context (not delegated as subagent) after /sync-docs completes. If the reviewer CLI is unavailable, silently skips and proceeds to /pr. Findings are triaged by the driving CLI using implementation context before presentation to the user.

name: cross-review
description: Use when the user wants two model vendors to review a change and then check each other's findings — «перекрёстное ревью», «пусть Claude и Codex проверят друг друга», «устрой спор / дебаты моделей», «cross-review», «debate review», «повтори обсуждение после правок» — over a branch, range, PR/MR, package, uncommitted work or an existing review run. Claude and Codex review with the same lenses, then cross-examine, answer objections and leave the disputes to a moderator. Not for a single-model review.

name: cross-review
description: The fresh reviewer pass for a code diff, run by the model family that did not write it, the Codex reviewer seat from a Claude session and the Claude reviewer seat from a Codex session, dispatched as configured, or by that family's own seat where the repository runs one runtime; and the plan review of a plan-first card, run by the other family before any build, with declared exceptions.

name: cross-review
description: 透過 herdr 另開 pane，以 Claude Code (Opus) 或 Devin CLI 跑 spec-reviewer / strict-reviewer 交叉審查；主 session 只負責修正，直到外部審查 PASS 才由執行端 session 做最後一次審查（實作情境為實作 pane 跑 strict-reviewer，主 session 不審）。使用者說「交叉審查」「送審」「cross-review」時使用。

name: cross-review

name: cross-review
description: 跨模型第二意見 PR review workflow（different-family reviewer dispatch、sticky comment write-back、merge gate enforcement）。使用時機：使用者 invoke /devpro:cross-review、要求對 PR 提供第二意見、要求跑 cross-model review，或 PR 需要 Step 5.5 post-PR review dispatch。

name: cross-review
description: Review the work on dev (or a given range) that the other agent wrote, against this repo's AGENTS.md rules and the shared memory's traps. Read-only: reports findings, edits nothing. Use when the user says cross-review, review Codex's work, review Claude's work, check the diff before merging to main.

name: cross-review

Produces a short findings file for AC to comment on; makes no edits. Use when: cross-review, second opinion, sense check this, run cross-review, GPT review.

name: cross-review

The owner can join the thread and steer. Use only when the operator asks for it (/cross-review or an explicit request); never start one on your own.

name: cross-review
description: Open a visible T3 review thread where a second model (Astra Extra High for a Claude author, Opus for a Codex author) reviews a plan or change, then go back and forth in that thread until both accept the same version. The owner can join the thread and steer. Use for /cross-review, for plans, finite primitive lists, authorization contracts and other architecture decisions.

Use as step 5 of /delivery:task, or when the user asks to "review this branch with Codex" or for a cross-model review. READ-ONLY: findings come from Codex; Claude applies fixes only when asked.

name: cross-review

name: cross-review

Use for /cross-review, 'cross-review this', 'have Sol review this', 'second model on this diff', or before calling auth, RLS, money, migration, or schema work done.

name: cross-review
description: Review a committed change with two independent models, adjudicate findings using evidence, and report within explicit budgets. Review-only by default; optionally repair and verify focused findings when authorized.

name: cross-review
description: draft 出来后 Claude (执笔) × GPT (critic) × Gemini (second critic) 三家互审，收敛到 final draft。固化你已经在 sub-agent 模式手动干的事。用户说 'cross review' / '互审' / '三家审' / 'codex review' 时调用。

name: cross-review
description: Cross-review a plan, a bug diagnosis, or a finished diff with independent read-only reviewers from two model families (Claude and Codex; models and effort from .AI/cross-review.conf, overridable per person), fanned out over several perspectives, iterated to consensus. Recommended, not required: offer it for non-trivial finished changes, for plans touching a risk subsystem in .AI/flow.md §3, and for disputed root causes, and run it when the user asks or agrees, including whenever the user asks to 검증/체크/교차검증/크로스리뷰 something. Works identically from a Claude or a Codex primary.

name: cross-review
description: Run a bounded cross-model review of a change, a slice, a whole branch or a plan, under the product's review protocol, with evidence-backed blockers, two rounds, and a decision page for the owner when it can't settle. Use before committing a slice, before merging a branch, for a plan review, or when asked to review or get a second model's verdict on work.

name: cross-review

Use after implementing anything important, before asking to merge.
