Attributes each changed file to Claude, Codex, or a human (via git trailers + Claude/Codex transcripts on disk), then routes Claude-written code to `codex exec` and Codex-written code to a fresh `claude -p`, runs both in parallel, and merges the findings. Use when the user asks for a cross-model / second-model review, wants "codex to review this", wants an independent reviewer that didn't author the code, or asks who wrote a diff. For a normal same-model review use /code-review.

name: cross-review
description: Use for cross-model review of code, diffs, branches, or PRs, including AI finding triage and bounded review-and-fix loops. For non-code artifacts, use cross-check.

name: cross-review
description: Use when a plan, design, document or diff would benefit from a review by a model from a different family before it is committed, or when the user asks for a second opinion, a cross-model review or an adversarial review.

name: cross-review
description: 担当交代後、既存物を変更する前に関連範囲と依存先をレビューする。説明・調査は止めない。全体レビューの明示依頼は全範囲を確認する。レビューと修正の依頼範囲を区別する。

name: cross-review
description: 跨工具交叉评审（Hermes 写 / Codex 审，或反之）。触发场景：一个 agent 或一个人写完了 一个 PR 需要另一个执行体审查、要给评审者准备 diff 与判据、评审意见来回拉扯需要裁决、 想知道评审该按什么规则说什么格式。

name: cross-review

name: cross-review
description: Cross-model adversarial code review. State the change's intent, dispatch independent reviewer agents on a different model family, each with one axis (correctness, spec, standards) and one lens (skeptic, architect, minimalist), then rule on each finding and re-review only the delta. Runs on interactive panes when herdr-core is present, print-mode CLIs otherwise, and a same-harness subagent as a declared last resort. Use when the user wants an adversarial review, a second opinion, a review by another agent or another model, or a review panel.

name: cross-review

Sends the same text, in parallel, to the LLM council (GPT, Gemini, Grok, Claude via OpenRouter) and to OpenAI Codex in a read-only sandbox, then merges both answers into one table of findings. Codex is optional; without the codex CLI it is a council-only review. Use when the user says "cross-review", "council and codex", "llm council and an adversarial codex", "have the other models check this plan", "check with the council and Codex whether option A is the best", or wants a plan stress-tested by several vendors before acting. Spends the user…

name: cross-review
description: Cross-family code review loop via T3 Code delegation against Standards, Spec, and test discipline until approved or stuck. Use as the review step after implementation, or when the user asks for a cross-review of a branch or PR.

name: cross-review
description: Use when asked for a review, or before shipping a large change. A model of another family reviews blind, as deeply as the change's risk calls for, then one round of fixes.

name: cross-review

name: cross-review
description: 指定された GitHub プルリクエストを、Claude と Codex の 2 モデルでクロスレビューし、 指摘を修正して再レビューする。1 ラウンド目は全重要度、2 ラウンド目以降は前ラウンドの 指摘の解消と新しい blocker だけを対象に、両モデルが揃って収束するまで上限 3 ラウンドで 繰り返してコミット・push する。 同じレビュー観点（docs/review-perspectives/）を両モデルに渡し、両方が指摘した箇所は 確度が高いものとして優先して対応する。Claude・Codex のどちらかが使えない（未インストール・ 未認証・呼び出し失敗）場合は、その旨をユーザーに伝えたうえで使える側だけの自己レビューに 縮退して処理を続ける（停止しない）。引数で PR 番号/URL を受け取り、無ければ対象 PR を ユーザーに確認する。ユーザーが「この PR をクロスレビューして」「claude と codex の両方で レビューして」「二重レビューで直して」「別モデルにもレビューさせて」などと言ったとき、または /za:cross-review を実行したときに使う。za:review の 2 モデル版なので、レビューの見落としを 減らしたい話が出たら積極的に使う。

name: cross-review
description: Audit a repository, file, directory, symbol, or diff with independent reviewers and agreed fixes. Use for cross review, cross review src/api.ts, cross review the reorder function, 全仓审查, or 交叉审查.

name: cross-review
description: Independent review via Codex or subagent.

description: Run builds, tests and linters through `crux <command>` (cargo, go test, pytest, tsc, make, gcc, javac, npm …) to get only the verdict, test counts, and errors/failures with file:line locations instead of hundreds of lines of output. The full output is saved to a log file. Use for any command whose output you only need to judge pass/fail and find problems.

name: crux
description: Turns a long video or podcast transcript into a compact, agent-ready "transcript pack" — a structured bundle (title, summary, chapters[], key_quotes[], outline) that minimises token usage while preserving meaning. Accepts a YouTube URL, a transcript file, or pasted transcript text.

name: crux-api
description: Use when querying Chrome UX Report field data, comparing lab vs field metrics, tracking Core Web Vitals trends, or correlating performance with search rankings. Also use when verifying CWV pass rates or checking p75 thresholds.

name: crux-audit
description: Use when the user says "/crux-audit" or wants a full coding-convention review of generated or existing TS/TSX code against all fourteen rule docs (the four post-code-audit judgment rules plus the ten path-scoped/global mechanical rules). Also use when the user says "/crux-audit install" to wire this skill's bundled routing table into a project or global CLAUDE.md for inline, path-scoped enforcement. Audit mode is report-only; it surfaces issues, never edits code, and leaves remedies to a dedicated refactoring agent; install is the one action permitted to create or edit a CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.loca…

name: crux-autopilot
description: Set up a crux autopilot search with the PI: write auto/<qid>/plan.md (question, editable paths, frozen scorer, objective), run `crux auto check`, and hand over the `crux auto run` line; never starts the run. Triggers: "set up an autopilot run", "start the autopilot", "write me an auto plan", crux auto.

name: crux-cockpit
description: Launch, check, stop or restart the crux cockpit, the read-only browser view of a crux vault (`crux serve`), locally or over SSH, and hand the user one URL. Triggers: "open the cockpit", "show me the tree in a browser", "is the cockpit running", "stop the cockpit", crux gui.

name: crux-config
description: Configure a project's CRUX workflow (roles, statuses, levels, agents, skills, retro) by interview and ship it as a .crux/ package. Started only by a project admin who runs crux-config [<stage> | edit <agent|flow|level>] in the project checkout. Writes .crux/ stage by stage, validates it, and opens a PR the new workflow starts from once merged.

name: crux-configuring
description: Use when the user wants to set up, configure, or troubleshoot Crux (ALCF) — SSH access, the embedding endpoint for docs search (RAG), or the ~/.hpc-agent/crux.json file. Also use when crux tools fail with connection or embedding errors.

name: crux-decisions
description: List all active decisions tracked by Crux with their rationales and constraints

name: crux-demo
description: Interactive demo of Crux (ALCF) — walks through configuration, facility info, live cluster status, docs search, filesystem access, and a real job end to end.

name: crux-diagnosis
description: Identify the pivotal obstacle between current state and desired future. Use when developing strategy.

name: crux-dispatch
description: Batch-start pipeline agent sessions for a CRUX role. Use when the user runs crux-dispatch <role> (e.g. crux-dispatch developer) or asks to start/dispatch the pipeline sessions for a role. Lists the role's tickets to pick from, claims each picked (ticket, agent) and opens one new session per pick that fetches its own agent prompt.

name: crux-export
description: Export current session decisions to CLAUDE.md. Use when the user wants to persist architectural decisions beyond the current session.

name: crux-init
description: Set up CRUX Compress in the current project from this plugin. Copies the CRUX specification to CRUX.md, adds or refreshes the <CRUX> block in AGENTS.md, records the version in .crux/crux.json, and optionally creates the memory system scaffolding. Use when CRUX.md is missing, after updating the plugin, or when the user asks to install, initialise, or update CRUX in a project.

name: crux-install
description: Make the crux command available, installing it only if it is missing. Use when another skill reports that `crux` is not on PATH, or when the user asks to install, update or upgrade the ideamans CrUX CLI. Prefers an already-installed binary, then the latest GitHub release, then a build from source with go install.

name: crux-litsearch

Triggers: "what am I missing in the literature", "find papers for this", "who else has done this", crux lit.

name: crux-memory-custody
description: Route OpenClaw memory reads and writes through a local Crux daemon so every memory carries a tamper-evident, verifiable record — and can be scanned for MemGhost-style poisoning. Local-first and free.

name: crux-monitoring-jobs
description: Use when the user asks about the status, progress, output, history, or failure of jobs on Crux (ALCF), or about queue and node availability. Also use this any time you (the agent) need to check on or wait for a job you submitted, even without a fresh user request.

name: crux-performance-audit
description: Analyze CrUX Vis PDFs, CrUX History data, and PageSpeed/Core Web Vitals evidence to identify when performance changed and what likely caused it.

name: crux-rd
description: Write the Requirements Document (RD) for a crux node: the settled design detail too long for the node, as one immutable page in rd/; a design change is a new RD that supersedes the old. Invoke explicitly, when the PI says a design has settled.

name: crux-reference
description: Use to answer questions about Crux (ALCF) itself — hardware, partitions, storage, software, policies, or where to get help. Ground answers in the bundled guide and live tool output rather than prior knowledge.

name: crux-release
description: Release a new Crux version end-to-end — version bump, quality gates (dart analyze / dart test), CHANGELOG, local release build, annotated git tag, push, and GitHub Release verification. Use when asked to release/publish/ship a version (e.g. "发布 0.15.0", "cut a release", "bump version"), when doing a local release build, or when auditing the release pipeline (install.sh, release.yml, build_release.dart).

name: crux-remote-command
description: Use when the user wants to run one or more shell commands on Crux (ALCF)'s login node, or when another workflow needs run_command_on_cluster for a live check not covered by a safer typed tool. Requires an exact command preview and explicit user permission before execution.

name: crux-reproducing
description: Use when the user asks to make a result on Crux (ALCF) reproducible, shareable, or turned into a notebook/script — or proactively suggest it after a chunk of exploratory job/file work that produced something worth preserving. Builds a Jupyter notebook that replays the real workflow via hpc_agent_core.client, not a hand-copied SSH script.

name: crux-retro
description: Run a CRUX retrospective over one sprint or date range in the project checkout. Use when the user runs crux-retro [<sprint> | --from YYYY-MM-DD --to YYYY-MM-DD] or asks for a sprint retro or a retrospective of the last week. Gathers the period's tickets, bugs and review artifacts from CRUX, follows the project's retro instructions, optionally runs paired A/B benchmarks, turns the recommendations the person picks into tickets and saves the retro.

name: crux-run
description: Start ONE pipeline agent session for a CRUX ticket. Use when the user runs crux-run <KEY>-N <agentKey> (e.g. crux-run CR-803 developer) or asks to start a specific ticket with a specific pipeline agent. Claims the step, then opens a new session whose first action fetches its own agent prompt.

name: crux-run-timeline

Output: timeline.html.

name: crux-skill-memory-crud

name: crux-skill-memory-index

name: crux-skill-memory-rebalance
description: Consolidate, promote, demote, and archive memories based on strength, usage patterns, and type transition rules. Use when running REM sleep, rebalancing memory strength, detecting conflicts, or cleaning up orphaned trackers.

name: crux-skill-memory-reference-tracker
description: Track which memories are referenced in agent output, manage .refs.yml tracker files, and keep strength counters in sync with memory frontmatter. Use when recording a memory reference, cleaning up orphaned trackers during REM sleep, or checking whether a memory should be promoted to a permanent rule.

name: crux-spec-coverage
description: Systematically evaluates whether specifications adequately cover their claimed capabilities, behaviors, scenarios, boundaries, failure conditions, and acceptance criteria, and prioritizes the gaps that matter most. name: crux-spec-deep-dive

name: crux-spec-distill

name: crux-spec-impact

name: crux-status

name: cursor-principle-explain-the-number

name: cursor-principle-fix-root-causes

name: cursor-principle-foundational-thinking

name: cursor-principle-laziness-protocol

name: cursor-principle-make-operations-idempotent
description: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.

name: cursor-principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis

name: cursor-principle-minimize-reader-load

name: cursor-principle-subtract-before-you-add

name: cutile-guide

name: cutile-persistent-matmul-gb10
description: Persistent kernels keep a tile block alive and process multiple output tiles in a strided loop. This is the dominant pattern for peak GEMM throughput in cuTile.

name: cutile-python

name: cutile-python-gb10

name: cutit
description: Apply a token-efficiency protocol to agentic coding work — narrow before reading, delegate open-ended search, cap tool output, edit instead of rewrite — so the same task finishes on fewer tokens with no drop in correctness. Invoke at the start of any non-trivial coding task, or explicitly via /cutit. Load references/checklist.md before a large read/search/write when unsure if it's warranted; load references/techniques.md for the rationale behind a rule.

name: cutit-agent-reuse
description: Catches spawning a brand-new sub-agent for follow-up work when an earlier one you already spawned is still idle and holds the exact context needed — a fresh spawn re-derives everything the idle one already knows. Invoke when a follow-up task relates to a sub-agent you spawned earlier in the same session.

name: cutit-artifact-reuse
description: Catches regenerating an entire document, artifact, or file from scratch when the user asked for a small, localized tweak to one already produced. Invoke whenever a follow-up request modifies something already generated rather than asking for something new.

name: cutit-assertion-first
description: Catches the pattern of generating a full solution before establishing what "correct" looks like, so a wrong turn only surfaces after a long elaboration has already been built on it. Invoke before writing a nontrivial solution, function, or multi-step answer whose correctness can be stated as a check up front.

name: cutit-backend
description: Catches backend-specific token waste — unbounded query results, full schema/log dumps, verbose stack traces past the first project frame, whole request/response bodies pulled in to check one field. Invoke when working on an API, database, server logs, or a migration.

name: cutit-background-task-batching
description: Catches polling a long-running background task every few seconds "to stay on top of it" — invoke whenever you've just started a background process or agent and are deciding when to check it next.

name: cutit-backoff-without-context-bloat
description: Catches re-appending the same failed request/output/error block into context on every retry attempt during a backoff loop, letting an N-attempt retry cost N times the tokens of one. Invoke when writing or driving any retry-with-backoff loop.

name: cutit-batch-vs-realtime
description: Catches bulk, non-urgent work (large-scale classification, log summarization, dataset transforms) being run through a real-time/interactive call path when a batch or async path would do the same job for less, and without occupying the interactive budget. Invoke when a task item-count is large and no immediate response is required.

name: cutit-breadth-vs-depth
description: Catches running a broad multi-file exploration when the target is already well specified — a named file, function, or error message that points at one place. Invoke when the request names a specific symbol/file/path instead of describing an area to explore.

name: cutit-cache-aware-prompting
description: Catches prompt structures that invalidate the provider's prefix cache on every call — invoke when assembling a prompt template that mixes stable instructions with per-call variables, especially in a loop that calls the same model repeatedly.

name: cutit-cheap-guardrail-first
description: Catches sending every output through an expensive model-based safety/quality check when a cheap rule-based check (regex, schema validation, keyword list, length bound) would already catch most violations. Invoke when designing or running a guardrail pipeline that has both rule-based and model-based checks available.

name: cutit-cheap-precheck
description: Catches the habit of launching a full test suite or manual end-to-end verification before running the lint/type-check/smoke-test that would have caught the same bug in seconds. Invoke before any expensive verification pass on a change that hasn't been syntax- or type-checked yet.

name: cutit-checkpoint-planning
description: Catches restarting a long multi-step task from step one after a mid-task failure, re-doing and re-verifying already-completed work instead of resuming from where it broke. Invoke when planning a long-running or many-step task that could fail partway through.

name: cutit-chunk-sizing
description: Catches the reflex of retrieving maximal chunk sizes "to be safe" — invoke when configuring or calling a retrieval/chunking step and picking how much surrounding text to pull per hit.

name: cutit-citation-scoping
description: Catches returning an entire source document when only the cited passage was needed — invoke whenever a retrieval or citation step is about to hand a full document back to the model instead of the specific span that supports the answer.

name: cutit-clarify-before-commit
description: Catches the pattern of guessing at an underspecified request and executing the full task on that guess, only to redo it at full cost once the user corrects the assumption. Invoke when a request has a genuine fork in interpretation before any code is written or files are searched.

name: cutit-config-reuse
description: Catches re-querying environment or configuration facts (package manager, framework version, working directory, env vars) at every step of a task when the session already established them earlier. Invoke before any step that would re-check a fact already confirmed this session.

name: cutit-confirmation-batching
description: Catches the pattern of asking the user to confirm one small decision at a time across several round-trips, when the decisions are known upfront and could be resolved in a single combined question. Invoke when a plan surfaces more than one point that needs user sign-off before or during execution.

name: cutit-consensus-minimalism
description: Catches the pattern of having cross-checking agents each re-derive a full independent solution when comparing compressed verdicts would settle agreement just as reliably. Invoke when multiple agents verify or vote on the same output and full re-derivation isn't what the comparison actually needs.

name: cutit-context-budget-tracking
description: Catches running a long task without any awareness of remaining context headroom, so a hard limit forces an abrupt mid-task truncation — invoke periodically during any long-running or many-turn task.

name: cutit-context-handoff
description: Catches pasting the full parent transcript (or an entire file/log) into a sub-agent's prompt "so it has everything," when the sub-task only needs a fraction of it — the rest is pure re-processing cost paid by a model that has to read it before doing anything. Invoke when writing the prompt or briefing for a spawned sub-agent.

name: cutit-context-injection-scoping
description: Catches serializing an entire object (a full API response, a whole database row, a complete config struct) into context when the agent only needs a few fields from it — invoke when injecting structured data from code into a prompt.

name: cutit-cross-turn-dedup
description: Catches redoing a search, computation, or file read from an earlier turn because a later user message asks for something that's actually already been produced or is derivable from it. Invoke when a new request sounds similar to something already done earlier in the conversation.

name: cutit-delegation-threshold
description: Catches indecision about whether to spawn a sub-agent, resolved by gut feel instead of a concrete rule — leading to either delegating trivial work (paying cold-start cost for nothing) or doing sprawling exploration inline (flooding your own context). Invoke at the moment of deciding whether a sub-task should be delegated.

name: cutit-dependency-ordering
description: Catches plans that run an expensive step before a cheap check that could have invalidated the whole plan — wasting the expensive step's tokens on a premise that was never going to hold. Invoke when ordering independent steps in a plan, before executing any of them.

name: cutit-design
description: Catches design-work token waste — reading a whole design system, style guide, or architecture doc to find one token or decision, re-describing a full Figma file or spec instead of its diff. Invoke when doing UI/UX design work (design tokens, components, Figma handoff) or system/architecture design (ADRs, design docs, API/interface contracts).

name: cutit-diff-only-output
description: Catches printing an entire file or object's before-and-after state to show an edit — invoke whenever you're about to report a change and could show just the delta instead.

name: cutit-diff-verification
description: Catches the reflex of re-reading an entire file to confirm an edit landed correctly when the diff itself already shows everything that changed. Invoke right after an edit, before deciding whether to re-read the file to check it.

name: cutit-difficulty-based-routing
description: Catches the default of running every subtask on the same top-tier model, even the mechanical ones (formatting, extraction, boilerplate scaffolding) that a cheaper model handles just as well. Invoke when a multi-step task contains subtasks whose difficulty clearly varies.

name: cutit-dynamic-prompt-assembly
description: Catches shipping one static maximal prompt template that includes every possible section on every call — invoke when designing a prompt template that serves more than one task variant or mode.

name: cutit-early-termination
description: Catches running the remainder of a fixed plan on autopilot after the actual goal has already been satisfied by an earlier step — the leftover steps produce no additional value but still cost tokens. Invoke after any step in a multi-step plan, to check whether the original goal is already met.

name: cutit-error-triage-budget
description: Catches pasting an entire stack trace, build log, or test-runner dump into context when only the last few frames or the first failing assertion are relevant. Invoke whenever a failing command's raw output is longer than a screen and hasn't been triaged yet.

name: cutit-escalation-on-failure
description: Catches the reflex of defaulting straight to the most expensive model or highest-effort attempt "to be safe," when a cheap attempt would have succeeded most of the time. Invoke when starting a task whose difficulty is unknown and a cheap first try is verifiable.

name: cutit-explore-then-commit
description: Catches open-ended exploratory search that keeps going round after round looking for a "better" candidate instead of committing once a good-enough one turns up. Invoke when a search for a target (file, config, existing helper) has run more than two rounds without a clear miss.

name: cutit-external-state-over-recap
description: Catches re-typing a natural-language summary of the plan or progress-so-far into the conversation each turn instead of holding it in structured task tracking. Invoke on any multi-step task where the current status would otherwise need restating in prose.

name: cutit-fail-fast-guardrails
description: Catches running expensive downstream pipeline steps before the cheapest guardrail check has had a chance to reject bad input, wasting every step that ran before the eventual rejection. Invoke when ordering a multi-stage pipeline that includes both cheap checks and expensive processing steps.

name: cutit-failure-scoped-logging
description: Catches capturing an entire test/CI run's logs when only the failing case's slice is needed to diagnose it. Invoke when pulling logs after a run that had both passing and failing parts.

name: cutit-fan-in-summarization
description: Catches reading each returned sub-agent result in full one at a time and re-summarizing after every one, instead of collecting all results and synthesizing once — repeated partial summarization re-processes the same growing context on every pass. Invoke when multiple sub-agents spawned in parallel are returning results that need to be combined.

name: cutit-few-shot-trimming
description: Catches padding a prompt with more or longer few-shot examples than the task needs to hit target accuracy — invoke when assembling or reviewing a few-shot prompt template.

name: cutit-frontend
description: Catches frontend-specific token waste — reading compiled/bundled output instead of source, un-filtered devtool/console logs, whole-stylesheet reads to find one rule, full-page DOM dumps to verify a small visual change. Invoke when working on UI components, styles, or a frontend build/dev-server issue.

name: cutit-function-calling-minimalism
description: Catches tool/function signatures carrying optional parameters, verbose descriptions, or redundant fields that get paid on every single call — invoke when designing or reviewing a tool schema before it ships.

name: cutit-goal-scoping
description: Catches over-delivering on a vague request — reading, searching, or building far more than the ask requires because the boundary was never pinned down. Invoke when a request is ambiguous in scope, before starting any exploration or execution.

name: cutit-golden-path-testing
description: Catches the pattern of exhaustively verifying edge cases before confirming the primary path even works, spending tokens on inputs nobody has hit yet while the common case sits unchecked. Invoke when deciding what to verify first after implementing a change.

name: cutit-graceful-degradation
description: Catches escalating spend (bigger model, more retries, deeper search) chasing an ideal approach that's failing, when a cheaper fallback would satisfy the actual requirement. Invoke when a preferred method has failed once or twice and a simpler alternative exists.

name: cutit-handoff-summarization
description: Catches the pattern of forwarding a raw transcript between agents or pipeline stages instead of a compressed summary of what the receiving side actually needs. Invoke at every agent-to-agent or stage-to-stage handoff before deciding what to pass along.

name: cutit-idle-agent-reuse
description: Catches spawning a brand-new sub-agent for a follow-up task when a recently completed or paused agent already holds the relevant context — invoke before any Agent call, to check for a resumable prior agent first.

name: cutit-incremental-validation
description: Catches the pattern of running every step of a multi-step task back to back and only checking output at the end, where an early failure has already compounded through later steps built on it. Invoke when executing a task with more than two sequential steps, each depending on the last.

name: cutit-instruction-dedup
description: Catches the same instruction being stated in the system prompt, repeated in the user message, and repeated again in a tool description — invoke when assembling a multi-message prompt (system + user + tool schemas) for a task.

name: cutit-known-failure-shortcuts
description: Catches re-diagnosing an error from scratch when its signature (message, error code, stack shape) matches one already solved earlier this session or documented in the project. Invoke as soon as an error message appears — check it against known signatures before starting fresh investigation.

name: cutit-known-location-shortcuts
description: Catches searching for something that has a well-known conventional location instead of going straight there — config files, migration folders, entry points, CI definitions. Invoke when the target is a project-convention artifact rather than arbitrary user code.

name: cutit-lazy-tool-loading
description: Catches the habit of resolving a deferred tool's full schema the moment it's mentioned, instead of at call time — invoke when a tool listing shows names-only entries you don't need yet.

name: cutit-long-task-progress-compaction
description: Catches keeping the full detail of a finished phase in context after it's no longer actionable — invoke right after any phase of a multi-step task completes, before moving to the next one.

name: cutit-memory-scoping
description: Catches pulling an entire memory store into context when a query only needs the entries relevant to this turn — invoke whenever a memory/notes/preferences system is queried.

name: cutit-memory-write-discipline
description: Catches writing everything learned during a task into persistent memory, including facts trivially re-derivable from the code or logs already in the repo. Invoke before any write to a persistent memory/notes file.

name: cutit-metric-first-triage
description: Catches opening individual failing cases one by one before checking what the aggregate metrics already say about where the problem concentrates. Invoke when a run produces both a metrics summary and per-case detail, before drilling into any single case.

name: cutit-multi-hop-retrieval-budget
description: Catches unbounded chaining in multi-hop retrieval loops — invoke when a retrieval step's output is about to trigger another retrieval step ("follow this reference," "look up what X depends on") without a hop cap.

name: cutit-multi-session-continuity
description: Catches persisting a full transcript or exploration log for a future session to read back in, when only a handful of durable facts are actually needed to pick the work back up — invoke when ending a session on a task that will continue later.

name: cutit-negative-result-shortcut
description: Catches exhaustively checking every remaining location to "prove" a negative when the question was already answered by the first authoritative miss. Invoke when a search is being used to confirm something does NOT exist, isn't referenced, or isn't the cause.

name: cutit-no-restate
description: Catches opening a response by paraphrasing the user's request or re-summarizing a plan that was just agreed on — invoke right before the first sentence of any answer, especially after a plan or clarifying exchange.

name: cutit-orchestrator-lean
description: Catches an orchestrator that delegates a sub-task but then also independently reads the same files or re-derives the same findings itself "just to be sure" — the work ends up held in two contexts instead of one. Invoke whenever you delegate a task, immediately after the sub-agent is spawned or has returned.

name: cutit-parallel-delegation
description: Catches spawning independent sub-agents one at a time, waiting for each to finish before starting the next, when they don't depend on each other — serial spawns cost the same total tokens but add wall-clock and re-orientation overhead each time you resume. Invoke when a plan has two or more sub-tasks that don't depend on each other's output.

name: cutit-partial-retry
description: Catches re-running an entire multi-step task from step one after only the last step failed, redoing work that already succeeded. Invoke when a pipeline, script, or plan with multiple steps fails partway through.

name: cutit-pipeline-caching
description: Catches the pattern of recomputing a pipeline stage's output on every run even when none of that stage's inputs changed since the last run. Invoke when a pipeline re-executes on repeated or incremental invocations and some stage's inputs are frequently unchanged.

name: cutit-pipeline-short-circuit
description: Catches the pattern of running every downstream stage of a pipeline even when an early stage's own check already fully answers the request. Invoke when designing pipeline control flow, or when a stage's output would make the remaining stages' work moot.

name: cutit-pipeline-stage-isolation
description: Catches the pattern of forwarding a pipeline's entire upstream history into each new stage when that stage only needs the immediately prior output. Invoke when designing or wiring a multi-stage agent pipeline where later stages receive more than the previous stage's result.

name: cutit-plan-caching
description: Catches re-deriving a plan from first principles for a task shape you've already solved this session (or that the project defines a known recipe for) — the plan structure is reusable even when the specifics differ. Invoke when starting a task that matches a pattern you (or the project) have already planned before.

name: cutit-plan-revision
description: Catches the reflex of throwing out an entire multi-step plan and regenerating it from zero the moment scope shifts slightly — most of the original plan is still valid and re-deriving it is wasted tokens. Invoke whenever new information changes a plan that's already in progress or already written down.

name: cutit-precomputed-index-reuse
description: Catches re-scanning or re-summarizing the same codebase/document set for every new query in a session instead of building one index or summary up front and querying it repeatedly. Invoke when a session is likely to run multiple searches or questions over the same material.

name: cutit-preference-capture
description: Catches re-asking or re-deriving a preference the user already stated once (formatting style, tone, preferred tool, naming convention), instead of writing it to memory/config and reusing it silently in future turns and sessions. Invoke the moment a user states a durable preference, not just when you need it again.

name: cutit-proactive-compaction
description: Catches leaving a fully resolved sub-thread (a debugging detour, a completed subtask) sitting in full detail in context instead of summarizing it once it's done — invoke right after any sub-thread reaches a conclusion.

name: cutit-progressive-widening
description: Catches defaulting to a repo-wide search when a narrower scope (current directory, current module, file type matching the task) would likely hit first. Invoke at the start of any search where the task already implies a probable location.

name: cutit-prompt-cache-preservation
description: Catches an edit to a prompt's stable prefix (system instructions, fixed context) that silently invalidates a warm prompt cache for every call after it. Invoke before editing anything earlier in an assembled prompt than the newest per-call content.

name: cutit-query-rewriting
description: Catches the retry-loop pattern where a vague first-pass query returns weak results and triggers a second or third retrieval call — invoke before issuing a retrieval query built directly from raw user phrasing.

name: cutit-relevance-filtering
description: Catches carrying the full accumulated history into a step when only a fraction of it bears on that step — invoke before referencing "everything so far" to decide the next action.

name: cutit-rerank-before-stuff
description: Catches paying to include irrelevant retrieved candidates in the prompt when they could have been scored and dropped first — invoke whenever multiple retrieval candidates are about to be inserted into context ("stuffed") before the model reasons over them.

name: cutit-response-length-budgeting
description: Catches defaulting to a maximally thorough, multi-section answer regardless of how big the question actually is — invoke before drafting any response, to size it to the question first.

name: cutit-result-digestion
description: Catches a sub-agent handing its full raw transcript, file dumps, or exploration log back to the parent instead of a compressed summary — the parent then re-reads all of it, doubling the cost of everything the sub-agent already processed. Invoke when a delegated agent is about to report its results back to its caller.

name: cutit-result-memoization
description: Catches recomputing a deterministic result (a build, a query, a parsed file, a computed diff) a second time in the same session when the inputs haven't changed. Invoke before re-running any tool call whose output you already have from earlier in this session.

name: cutit-retrieval-caching
description: Catches re-running retrieval for a query the session already answered, or one close enough in meaning to reuse — invoke before issuing a retrieval call inside a loop that has run similar queries earlier in the same session.

name: cutit-retry-without-reload
description: Catches re-sending context that already made it into a failed tool call — invoke right after any tool call errors out and before constructing the retry.

name: cutit-role-specialization
description: Catches the pattern of giving every agent in a pipeline the same broad context and letting each one re-derive facts another agent already established. Invoke when defining agent roles or system prompts in a multi-agent pipeline.

name: cutit-rolling-summary
description: Catches keeping a long session's full turn-by-turn history live when a maintained running summary would carry the same load-bearing facts — invoke once a session has accumulated many resolved turns.

name: cutit-root-cause-first-retry
description: Catches the reflex of re-running a failed command or test unchanged and hoping for a different outcome, instead of reading the first failure closely enough to name why it happened. Invoke the moment a command fails and before issuing any retry.

name: cutit-sampled-eval-review
description: Catches reading every failing transcript in an eval run when a representative sample would surface the same failure modes at a fraction of the tokens. Invoke when an eval run produces more failing cases than are needed to identify distinct failure patterns.

name: cutit-scratchpad-offloading
description: Catches keeping large intermediate state (accumulated notes, partial results, a growing list) live in the prompt across many turns instead of writing it to a scratch file and reading back only what's needed — invoke whenever intermediate state needs to survive more than a couple of turns.

name: cutit-search-index-first

name: cx-workflow-calibration-lod

name: cx-workflow-callset-qc
description: Check cohort quality in an already-called synthetic small-variant genotype table using frozen filters, controls-only exact Hardy-Weinberg tests, trio consistency and X heterozygosity. Use for offline arithmetic checks of tab-free JSON fixtures; never for VCF parsing or variant interpretation.

name: cx-workflow-cell-count-viability
description: Check recorded hemocytometer or automated-counter cell counts with frozen chamber volumes, dilution, dye mixing, replicate agreement and exact live-fraction bounds. Use for supplied synthetic count tables; exclude culture-health, potency, release and medical conclusions.

name: cx-workflow-cfu-plate-counts

Use for synthetic count-table QC, guide log2 changes and gene summaries; exclude essentiality, drug targets and biological conclusions.

name: cx-workflow-ddpcr-absolute-quantification
description: Check already-read droplet digital PCR partition counts with frozen controls, Poisson copy concentration, exact binomial bounds and concordant replicate pooling. Use for supplied synthetic count tables; exclude copy-number state, gene dosage and medical conclusions.

name: cx-workflow-diagnostic-accuracy
description: Evaluate diagnostic accuracy of supplied per-subject continuous scores against a reference standard using frozen thresholds, bias refusals, Wilson intervals and tie-aware ROC AUC. name: cx-workflow-dissolution-profile-f2
description: Check supplied synthetic percent-dissolved profiles with frozen shared times, unit counts, CV limits and mean-based f1/f2 factors. Use for offline arithmetic; exclude bioequivalence, product quality and acceptance decisions.

name: cx-workflow-dose-response-curve
description: Fit in-vitro concentration-response curves with frozen assay declarations, labelled biological and technical replicates, control separation, constrained four-parameter logistic curves and potency intervals. Use for EC50 or IC50 evidence; never prescribing or patient benefit.

name: cx-workflow-enzyme-kinetics
description: Check Michaelis-Menten Vmax, Km, kcat and Jacobian uncertainty from supplied synthetic initial-rate fixtures under frozen linear-window and depletion rules; offline arithmetic only, with no inhibitor or biological claims.

name: cx-workflow-experiment-design
description: Conduct a fixed six-stage preregistered experiment-design procedure for lab or computational studies, from question and independent-unit power planning through randomisation, frozen analysis, controls and independent review handoff. Use before collection or for post-hoc audit; this pack does not run experiments or establish causal, physical or clinical validity.

name: cx-workflow-factorial-doe-effects

name: cx-workflow-flow-cytometry-qc
description: Check already-acquired synthetic flow cytometry event tables against frozen compensation, singlet, live/dead and channel gates; return control-qualified counts and parent-relative percentages. Use for offline cytometry QC arithmetic, never cell identity, function or disease interpretation.

name: cx-workflow-gene-set-overrepresentation

name: cx-workflow-growth-curve
description: Estimate per-well microbial or cell-culture OD growth rates, tangent lag, observed carrying-capacity proxy, integrated OD and doubling times from supplied synthetic time series. name: cx-workflow-gwas-summary-qc

name: cx-workflow-hplc-system-suitability
description: Check recorded replicate standard injections using frozen HPLC peak identities, retention-time and area RSD, tailing, plates, nearest-peak resolution and blank carryover. Use with synthetic peak tables; exclude method validation and release decisions.

name: cx-workflow-hts-plate-qc

name: cx-workflow-immunoassay-4pl
description: Check supplied plate immunoassay optical densities with a frozen four-parameter logistic standard curve, replicate controls, bracketed sample interpolation and dilution parallelism. Use for already-measured synthetic OD fixtures; exclude clinical interpretation and wet-lab execution.

name: cx-workflow-meta-analysis-evidence
description: Pool already-extracted study effects with frozen eligibility, cohort deduplication, comparable scales, heterogeneity and sensitivity gates. Use for quantitative evidence synthesis; use literature-review for retrieval. Never infer causality or patient care.

name: cx-workflow-metabolomics-feature-qc
description: Check an already-acquired untargeted LC-MS feature table using pooled QC, blanks, injection order and a dilution series before differential comparisons. Use for offline arithmetic checks of supplied synthetic intensities; never for compound identification or biomedical conclusions.

name: cx-workflow-microbiome-composition
description: Compare microbial community composition between two conditions from supplied sample-by-taxon integer counts. Use for 16S or shotgun taxon tables, CLR, diversity and stratified PERMANOVA; exclude sequence processing, absolute microbial load and medical decisions.

name: cx-workflow-nucleic-acid-quant-purity
description: Check supplied nucleic-acid absorbance readings with frozen dsDNA/RNA conversion factors, path length, dilution, A320 background, matched blank and purity-ratio bands. Use for synthetic spectrophotometric arithmetic; exclude sample suitability and downstream-use conclusions.

name: cx-workflow-particle-size-distribution
description: Check supplied binned particle diameters with frozen micrometre edges, cumulative D10/D50/D90, span, midpoint means and replicate agreement. Use for already-measured synthetic count or volume tables; exclude product quality, stability, performance and regulatory conclusions.

name: cx-workflow-peak-replicate-qc

name: daraja
description: This skill provides guidance for integrating Safaricom Daraja M-Pesa APIs. Use when the user asks about "M-Pesa", "Daraja API", "STK Push", "Lipa Na M-Pesa", "M-Pesa Express", "B2C payments", "C2B payments", "Safaricom API", "paybill integration", or needs help with M-Pesa authentication, callbacks, or transaction queries.

name: daraja-account-ops
description: Uses Safaricom Daraja's Transaction Status, Transaction Reversal and Account Balance APIs, whose results arrive asynchronously on a ResultURL, and builds reconciliation jobs on top of them. Use when resolving unknown or timed-out M-Pesa transactions, reversing a mistaken C2B payment, checking shortcode balances, or designing nightly reconciliation.

name: daraja-agent-storefront
description: Recipe for an AI agent that sells and takes M-Pesa payments for a store, either inside a developer-built store with its own backend or as an agent-only seller in a chat. Covers working out which kind of store it is, the order-to-STK-to-confirmed flow, using the order ID as the account reference, tracking orders with forwarding or a CSV sales log, safe retries after failed payments, receipts, and refunds behind approval. Use when an agent handles selling, checkout or order payments for a shop over chat, WhatsApp, a website assistant or similar.

name: daraja-auth
description: Generates, caches and refreshes Safaricom Daraja OAuth 2.0 access tokens from the Consumer Key and Secret (client-credentials grant with HTTP Basic auth), including single-flight refresh, 401 retry and multi-instance caching. Use when writing the token helper for any M-Pesa API, or when debugging 400.008.xx, 401 or 404.001.03 "Invalid Access Token" errors.

name: daraja-b2b
description: Implements Safaricom Daraja B2B payments between shortcodes: BusinessPayBill (to a Paybill and account), BusinessBuyGoods (to a Till), BusinessPayToBulk (top up a B2C utility account) and B2B Express Checkout (a USSD push asking a merchant's till operator to pay your Paybill). Covers identifier types, the initiator and SecurityCredential, and Result handling. Use when one business pays another business, a supplier, or its own disbursement account.

name: daraja-b2c
description: Implements Safaricom Daraja B2C payouts from a business shortcode to customers' M-Pesa wallets (BusinessPayment, SalaryPayment, PromotionPayment) and to Pochi la Biashara (B2Pochi). Covers the initiator and SecurityCredential, OriginatorConversationID idempotency, Result and QueueTimeOut callbacks, and result codes 2001, 2040, 8006 and 21. Use for refunds, salaries, withdrawals, winnings, commissions or any business-to-person disbursement.

name: daraja-bill-manager
description: Integrates M-Pesa Bill Manager through Safaricom Daraja. Covers opting a Paybill in, sending single or bulk SMS e-invoices with automatic reminders, receiving payment notifications, acknowledging them so customers get e-receipts, and cancelling or updating invoices. Use for invoicing and collections such as rent, school fees, utilities, SACCO dues or subscriptions where customers pay a Paybill against an account reference.

name: daraja-c2b
description: Implements Safaricom Daraja C2B (Customer-to-Business) for Paybill and Till numbers. Covers registering Validation and Confirmation URLs, accepting or rejecting payments with C2B00011-C2B00016 codes, recording confirmations idempotently, simulating in sandbox, and recovering missed payments with the Pull Transactions API. Use when customers pay from the M-Pesa menu or app and the system must record or validate those payments.

name: daraja-callbacks
description: Builds resilient Safaricom Daraja callback and webhook receivers: STK CallBackURL; C2B Validation and Confirmation; ResultURL and QueueTimeOutURL for B2C, B2B, tax, status, reversal and balance; Ratiba, Bill Manager and B2B Express callbacks. Covers fast acknowledgment, async processing, idempotency, payload parsing, endpoint security and the "callback never arrived" checklist. Use when writing or debugging any endpoint that M-Pesa posts results to.

name: daraja-checkout
description: End-to-end recipe for adding M-Pesa checkout to an existing web or mobile app with STK Push. Works out the stack, shortcode type and callback setup from the codebase and configuration, asks at most three questions, then builds the order-to-paid flow with a payments table, a callback route, a missing-callback query job and failure tests. Use when someone wants customers to pay for an order, cart, booking or invoice with M-Pesa in their app.

name: daraja-credentials-security
description: Manages Safaricom Daraja secrets safely (Consumer Key and Secret, M-Pesa Express passkey, initiator password, SecurityCredential) and generates the SecurityCredential by RSA-encrypting the initiator password with Safaricom's sandbox or production certificate. Covers .env files versus secret managers, fail-fast config, log masking, rotation and leak response. Use when wiring M-Pesa configuration, generating a SecurityCredential, or handling 2001, 18 or 8006 initiator errors.

name: daraja-dynamic-qr
description: Generates M-Pesa Dynamic QR codes with Safaricom Daraja for Buy Goods, Paybill, agent withdrawal, send money or send-to-business, with a preset amount and reference, and renders the returned base64 PNG. Use when building in-store, invoice, receipt or point-of-sale flows where customers scan with the M-Pesa or My Safaricom app to pay.

name: daraja-paybill-collections
description: End-to-end recipe for collecting payments that customers start themselves on a Paybill or Till (C2B), and matching them to accounts. Covers registering confirmation and validation URLs, account-number matching, orphan payments, Pull Transactions for missed callbacks, and the daily reconciliation report. Use when customers pay via the M-Pesa menu to a Paybill/Till and the business needs those payments matched to invoices, tenants, students or customer accounts.

name: daraja-payment-design
description: Designs the system around M-Pesa Daraja calls so money is never lost or double-counted. Covers the payment state machine, an append-only ledger with integer shillings and unique receipts, callback confirmation handling, reversals versus B2C refunds, daily reconciliation, failure testing in the sandbox, and a go-live checklist, plus a script that scans a codebase for common integration mistakes. Use when building or reviewing a payment integration, designing payment tables, handling confirmations, refunds or reconciliation, or preparing to go live.

name: daraja-payouts
description: End-to-end recipe for paying people from a business with M-Pesa B2C, such as payroll, commissions, supplier-to-wallet payments, winnings and refunds. Covers a payout batch table, idempotency keys, approvals, recipient allowlists, handling queue timeouts without double-paying, result callbacks, and float checks. Use when someone wants to send money to many phones, run salaries or disbursements, or build a refund flow.

name: daraja-ratiba
description: Creates M-Pesa Ratiba standing orders (recurring customer payments to a Paybill or Till) through Safaricom Daraja, including frequency codes, date rules, the PIN-consent prompt, and the callback that returns the TransactionID. Use for subscriptions, loan repayments, "Lipa Mdogo Mdogo" instalments, rent, school fees or any recurring M-Pesa collection.

name: daraja-recurring-billing
description: End-to-end recipe for subscriptions and recurring charges with M-Pesa Ratiba standing orders, with Bill Manager invoices or STK reminders as fallbacks. Covers customer consent, schedule and amount rules, tracking each collection, failed-charge handling and dunning, and cancelling. Use when someone wants monthly subscriptions, rent, school fees, loan repayments or any repeat payment collected automatically from M-Pesa customers.

name: daraja-sandbox-setup
description: Sets up a Safaricom Daraja sandbox from scratch: creating the developer account and app with the right products, finding test credentials (shortcodes, passkey, initiator, certificate), writing the .env file, exposing callbacks through a tunnel, smoke testing each API, and running the production go-live checklist. Use when starting a new M-Pesa integration, when a sandbox setup is broken, or when preparing to go live.

name: daraja-stk-push
description: Implements Safaricom M-Pesa Express (Lipa na M-Pesa Online / STK Push) and STK Push Query. Covers building the Password and EAT Timestamp, sending the PIN prompt to a customer's phone, handling the stkCallback, polling status, and acting on ResultCodes such as 1032, 1037 and 2001. Use for checkout or "pay now" flows where the business starts a payment the customer approves with their M-Pesa PIN.

name: daraja-tax-remittance
description: Remits taxes to the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) from a business shortcode through Safaricom Daraja's Tax Remittance API (CommandID PayTaxToKRA, PartyB 572572, AccountReference set to the KRA Payment Registration Number). Use when a system must pay KRA taxes such as VAT, PAYE or withholding tax via M-Pesa.

name: daraja-teach-me
description: An interactive tutor that teaches M-Pesa Daraja step by step in the sandbox. Offers a learning roadmap by category (foundations, collecting money, paying out, callbacks, operations, payment design) plus a build-your-own-gateway track, explains each idea in plain language with diagrams, then has the learner run a real sandbox call and checks their understanding. Refuses production credentials. Use when the user says "teach me", "explain M-Pesa", "I'm new to Daraja", "how does STK Push work", wants a tutorial or course, or wants to learn by building their own payment gateway.

name: daraja-troubleshooting
description: Diagnoses Safaricom Daraja and M-Pesa API failures. Decodes errorCodes (400.002.02, 404.001.03, 500.001.1001, 500.003.02...), async ResultCodes (1, 17, 1032, 1037, 2001, 2028, 2040, 8006...), C2B and reversal codes, missing callbacks and sandbox/production mix-ups, with a lookup script and a step-by-step debug procedure. Use when an M-Pesa request fails, returns an unexpected code, or a payment or callback never shows up.

name: daraz-api
description: Daraz Open Platform API integration. Use when working with Daraz marketplace APIs for product management, order processing, logistics, finance, returns, or any seller operations. Includes authentication (OAuth 2.0, HMAC signatures), API categories (Product, Order, Logistics, Finance, Return, etc.), base URLs by country, and common error codes.
